blocks.text: Play with keyboard and mouse. Keys here are defaults; change gameplay assignments in Settings > Controls > Key bindings. Keys follow physical positions, so on another keyboard layout use the QWERTY positions or assign keys that suit you. {{input-devices-and-layout}}

The window opens at 1280 × 720 and cannot be made smaller than 800 × 450. Press [[F11]] or [[Alt]] + [[Enter]] to toggle borderless fullscreen; the game does not remember fullscreen between launches. {{window-and-fullscreen}}
For installation, updating and finding worlds, see {{guide:install-and-worlds|Install, update and find your worlds}}. This page starts at the game’s menu.

blocks.alt: The Voxelgame start menu: a stone panel with brass corners over a view of forest and meadow, headed by the qiqi cube logo. Buttons read Continue, Worlds, Multiplayer, Structure workshop, Mods, Settings, Credits and Quit, with a keyboard hint line at the bottom.
blocks.caption: The start menu. Headless capture from a Voxelgame build of 8 November 2026 (1280 × 720, disposable seed-42 world).

blocks.text: Choose **Continue** to resume the loaded world or **Worlds** to choose or create one. Continue is unavailable when no usable world is loaded. **Multiplayer**, **Structure workshop**, **Settings**, **Credits** and **Quit** are also on the menu. {{start-menu}}

items: **Continue** resumes the loaded world.
**Worlds** lists saves and opens the creation dialog.
**Settings** opens graphics, audio, control and interface preferences.
**Credits** has seven cards. Use Left/Right or Previous/Next to browse; Tab selects a footer button, and Enter or Space activates it. Esc or Skip credits returns to the menu. {{credits}}

blocks.text: These steps cover the base game.

items: Choose **Worlds**, then **Create world**.
Enter a name. Leave Seed blank for a fresh seed or enter unsigned decimal digits to reuse a seed.
Choose **Creative** or **Survival**. Leave terrain generation at the current default unless you need an older one.
Choose **Create world** or press [[Enter]]. [[Esc]] or **Cancel** returns without creating a world.

blocks.text: A new world's pack contains 12 Berries, 2 Water flasks, 1 Empty flask and 4 Alder board pieces. Switching modes and respawning do not grant another starter pack. {{new-world-start}}

Select a world in the list, then choose **Play world**, press [[Enter]] or double-click its row. One click only selects it. For rename, duplicate, backup and recovery steps, see {{guide:install-and-worlds|Install, update and find your worlds}}. {{worlds-page}}
Star worlds you want to find quickly, then use the Starred filter. {{worlds-page}}

To delete a world, select it and hold **Delete world** (or the [[Delete]] key) for 3 seconds; letting go early cancels. Deleting removes the save for good and cannot be undone, so make a backup first with **Create backup**. The world you are currently in cannot be deleted. {{worlds-page}}

Click the world once to capture the mouse. That first click never mines or places a block. While the mouse is released (after opening a panel, pressing [[Esc]], or switching away from the window) you cannot move or look. Closing a panel captures the mouse again on its own. {{mouse-capture}}

rows: Walk forward, left, back, right (about 4.3 m/s). You step up half-metre blocks without jumping.
Jump about 1.25 m; hold it to jump again on every landing. A full one-metre block needs a jump.
Sneak at about 1.3 m/s; you cannot walk off an edge while sneaking.
Crawl through gaps 0.6 m tall; press C or Space again to stand.
Start or stop flying (creative only). Space rises, Shift descends, Ctrl boosts.

blocks.text: Leaves and needles do not block you. Walk into a tree crown at half speed, hold [[Space]] to climb up and [[Shift]] to climb down, or let go to stay where you are. You can stand on top of a crown; hold [[Shift]] as you land to sink into it. {{move-through-leaves}}
Walking speeds do not depend on frame rate, because movement runs on a fixed 60 Hz step. {{walk-and-look}}
The default **F10** key saves a game screenshot and reports the saved path. **Print Screen** releases the pointer for your system screenshot tool. {{clean-view}}

blocks.alt: First-person view over a hazy flowering meadow with a large tree. A status message is at the top left above a First steps goals card, a square compass map at the top right with a frames-per-second, coordinates and biome readout beneath it, a crosshair in the centre, the hand at the lower right and a row of ten empty hotbar slots at the bottom.
blocks.caption: The screen in a new creative world, with the optional First steps goals card open. Headless capture from a Voxelgame build of 8 November 2026 (1280 × 720, disposable seed-42 world).

items: **Top left:** the status line. Actions report here, for example 'Collected … ×3' or 'Capacity full; block left behind'.
**Top right, left of the map:** the looking-at card, shown when you aim at a block within 6 m. [[F2]] hides or shows it, the same as Settings > Interface > Layout > Target info.
**Top right:** the compact map, with the FPS and coordinates box beneath it. The box is on by default; turn it off in Settings > Advanced > Diagnostics.
**Lower right:** the collection feed. It shows what you gained, for example '+3 Oak wood', for a few seconds. Crafting, creative mining and home storage do not show there.
**Middle:** the crosshair, and a small action hint under it.
**Lower left (survival only):** the four bars for health, hunger, thirst and stamina.
**Bottom:** the ten-slot hotbar and the label of the selected item.

blocks.text: Press the default [[F1]] key to hide the HUD, crosshair and hands, then [[F10]] to save a screenshot. Press F1 again to restore the view. The pause menu also has **Screenshot**. {{clean-view}}

sections.title: Open your pack and the hotbar

blocks.alt: The creative inventory with the Catalogue tab open. Tab icons run along the top; Your pack lists a few carried items on the left with the selected Meadow turf below, and the right side shows a search field, category icons and a paged grid of block icons. The ten-slot hotbar sits below the panel.
blocks.caption: The creative Catalogue tab. Headless capture from a Voxelgame build of 8 November 2026 (1280 × 720, disposable seed-42 world). This build titles the load readout Capacity; the current game reads Load.

blocks.text: Press [[E]] to open or close the inventory. Switch tabs with the mouse, [[Tab]] or [[Shift]]+[[Tab]]. Creative has the free Build catalog; Survival carpentry adds Build when you carry a Furniture hammer. The pack holds up to 1000 capacity. The header at the top right shows your load, for example "Load: 0.1 / 1000". {{inventory-workspaces}} {{carry-capacity}}

Pack shows carried items as a paged icon grid. Hover for the name, quantity and help; click to use or equip an item. [[Ctrl]]+[[F]] searches by name, and the sort button switches between grouped and alphabetical order. Dragging inside Pack does not rearrange or split your stock. {{pack-items-list}} {{planned-inventory-overhaul}}
The hotbar
The hotbar has ten slots that start empty. A slot is a shortcut to an item kind, not a container, so its number is everything of that kind in your pack.

rows: Bind that item to the slot (inventory open).
Drag an item onto a slot
Bind it. Dragging a slot onto another swaps them; dragging a slot off the bar clears it.

blocks.text: With the inventory closed, [[Tab]] cycles through the tools and weapons you carry and back to empty hands. Your hotbar slot assignments are saved with the world. {{hotbar-quick-slots}}

In survival, [[J]] drops one selected carried item; [[Ctrl]]+[[J]] drops everything of that kind. With Pack open, hover its icon first. Approach a dropped stack after a short delay to collect what fits. {{planned-ground-drops}}

There are exactly two modes. Press [[F4]] to switch, except on the start menu, while joined to someone else's server, or while a stopped host waits for recovery. When you host a world, the switch happens once the server confirms it. Your pack, hotbar and position stay as they are, and each world remembers the mode you left it in. {{game-modes}}
Creative

items: Blocks break instantly and placing is free; crafting is free.
The Build tab and catalog, middle-click block picking, building brushes and undo.
Flight, map travel and teleport.
Editable time, weather and season.

blocks.text: Survival

items: Blocks take time to mine and your pack is limited to 1000 capacity.
Four bars for health, hunger, thirst and stamina, shown lower left.
Falls hurt, and you eat with [[R]], drink with [[T]] and quick-craft with [[X]].
Dying opens a screen showing the cause and respawn location. Press [[Enter]] or click **Respawn** when ready; you keep your inventory. {{death-respawn}}

blocks.text: Items you took from the creative catalog stay in your pack after you switch to survival. Continue with {{guide:first-survival-day|Your first survival day}}.

blocks.alt: The in-game Settings panel. Categories Graphics, Audio, Controls, Gameplay, Interface and Advanced are on the left; Graphics is open on its Display subpage, with rows for Graphics preset, Field of view, Horizon distance, Atmospheric fog, Frame limit, Shader and Chunk fade-in, and Reset page, Back and Resume buttons along the bottom.
blocks.caption: Settings opened from a world, Graphics > Display. Headless capture from a Voxelgame build of 8 November 2026 (1280 × 720, disposable seed-42 world). The debug capture uses its own view distance, so the preset reads Custom.

blocks.text: Press [[Esc]] for the pause menu, then choose **Settings**. Esc first closes an active panel or dialog. From in-game Settings, **Back** or Esc returns to the pause menu; **Resume** returns to play. Local play pauses; a connected server continues. {{settings-menu}} {{escape-and-pause}}

rows: Close the active panel or open the pause menu.

Save your local world, or the world you host, now ('World saved safely'). In a server world you joined, nothing is written on your computer and the game says 'This session does not save the world locally'.
Save and return to the start menu (pause menu).
Ctrl + Q, Save & quit or the window's close button
Save, then quit. If saving fails, the game stays open.

blocks.text: For autosaves, backups and recovery, see {{guide:saves|Saves and world files}}. Graphics, sound, interface settings and key bindings follow you between worlds; world time, weather and season remain local. {{saving-and-quitting}}

sections.title: The keys you will use most

rows: Walk. Fly horizontally in creative flight.
Look around, once you have clicked the world to capture the pointer.
Jump; rise while flying or swimming.
Sneak (ledge guard), dive, descend in flight, steady a ranged weapon. Hold it while mining or placing to work on one half-metre piece.
Mine or remove the block you aim at; hit an animal.
Place the held block (a block selected, no tool equipped); hold to draw a bow or wind up a throw. Also uses what you aim at: a door, chest, seat, bed or lamp.
Equip the next tool (inventory closed) or the next inventory tab (inventory open).
Close the active layer or open the pause menu.
Save now. In a server world you joined, nothing is saved on your computer and the game says so.

blocks.text: Sprint and sneak use held keys by default; crawl is a toggle. Change Hold/Toggle in Settings > Gameplay > Movement. {{input-devices-and-layout}}
Change a gameplay key

items: Open Settings > Controls > Key bindings.
Select an action with Up/Down and press Enter, or click its row to start capture. Previous/Next or Page Up/Page Down changes action page.
Press a physical key. Esc cancels capture; Delete leaves the action unbound.
If a conflict appears, choose another key or change the other action: shared assignments can trigger both. Reset keys or Backspace outside capture restores every default binding.

blocks.text: Esc, F6, F11 and Print Screen are reserved. Native shortcuts such as Alt+Enter and Ctrl+Q, menu navigation and text entry keep their physical keys. {{input-devices-and-layout}}

items: **Shift** is shared by default: sneak on the ground, dive in water, descend while flying, steady a bow or rifle, and work on one half-metre piece when you mine or place. In creative, **N** toggles half-metre building so you can release Shift. {{sneak-ledge-guard}} {{half-metre-detail-building}}
**Tab** equips tools when the inventory is closed and switches tabs when it is open. {{equip-tools-tab}}
**Z** zooms, but **Ctrl + Z** is undo, so Z does not zoom while Ctrl is held. It undoes furniture and chest refinishing steps in either mode, and building and door moves in creative. {{hold-to-zoom}}
**C** crawls on foot. In a boat, it cycles camera stations. {{crawl}}
**F** toggles flight in creative; in survival it only shows 'Flight is available in creative mode'. {{creative-flight}}
**F5** cycles first person, third person rear and third person front. The perspective is not saved. {{camera-perspectives}}
**B** cycles creative brushes, and in survival takes the Blueprint tool out. With a furniture plan out it puts the plan away instead, and it cancels a door move. {{creative-brush-cycle}}

blocks.text: Key names describe physical positions. On a non-QWERTY board, use those positions or reassign gameplay actions. {{input-devices-and-layout}}

Default keys. Survival needs a furniture hammer in your pack for plans; Creative does not. {{guide:furniture-and-carpentry|Furniture and carpentry}} and {{guide:storage-beds-and-lamps|Storage, beds and lamps}} explain each step; doors are in {{guide:building-basics|Building basics}}.
While a furniture plan is selected

rows: E, with a plan or the hammer in hand
Open the carpentry workbench. Aim at furniture first to change its woods, or at a placed chest to refinish it.
Place the furniture at the ghost. With only the hammer in hand, it opens the workbench instead.
Turn the ghost 90 degrees. Wall pieces: aim at a wall side and turn their back toward it.
Take up the aimed furniture. Empty its storage first.
Lock the aimed furniture to move it. R turns it, right click places it, left click cancels.
Join a floor kitchen piece to the side of the aimed one.
Undo / redo your last furniture step.

blocks.text: Using furniture (plan put away)

rows: Sit. Space or right click stands you up when the way is clear.
Lie down. Space or right click gets you up when the way is clear.
Switch it on or off (no tool or plan in hand).
Right click a chest or storage furniture
Open its storage. Click an item to move one; Shift + click moves as many of that item as fit.
Open its panel. Click moves one item, Shift + click as many as fit; Start cooks one batch.
Right click a table top, red lantern selected
Put the lantern on display. Works on tables, desks, bookcases and wall shelves. Ctrl + Z undoes it.
Right click the display, empty slot selected

blocks.text: Doors

rows: Copy its exact style, wood and size into your hand.
Shift + Left click a closed door (Creative)
Lock it to move. R turns it, right click places it, left click or B cancels. Ctrl + Z and Ctrl + Shift + Z undo and redo the move.

blocks.text: Home tab

rows: Arrow keys, Page Up / Page Down
Move between the actions and the carried and stored lists.
Use the selected action, or move the selected item. Shift moves as many as fit.

blocks.text: With a block or empty hands, aiming at furniture refuses mining ("Furniture blocks that mining target") and block placement ("Furniture blocks that placement"). On a server, wait for the server to confirm before the next furniture, bed, stove or door-move action.
Each row names the feature that owns it; follow the link for its summary and source evidence. Rows for developer tools or features still in development carry a status label.

guides.title: Your first survival day
guides.headline:
Your first survival day,
from berries to a home.
guides.summary: Read the four bars, drink, eat, mine, make stone tools, cook, build a home and recover after death.
guides.lead: What the four bars mean, what to do in the first minutes, which crafting chain gets you tools and a roof, and what can actually hurt you.

verification.method: Targeted source review on 5 November 2026 at Voxelgame aa136e0103ce5599c6d8a9f70c669dbc758b7357: starter quantities, Pack controls, manual item dropping and death/respawn, including the relevant source tests. blocks.text: Choose **Survival** when creating a world, or press [[F4]] in a local creative world to switch. You keep your pack, hotbar and position, and the four bars appear lower left. Every new world's pack holds 12 Berries, 2 Water flasks, 1 Empty flask and 4 Alder board pieces. Switching modes or respawning never grants more. {{new-world-start}}
Items you took from the creative catalog before switching stay in your pack, so start in a fresh world if you want a true first day.

rows: Health. It regenerates slowly while both hunger and thirst stay above 65.
A full bar lasts about 40 minutes.
A full bar lasts about 30 minutes.
Spent by sprinting, which needs more than 3% left. Resting at home refills it.

blocks.text: The bars do not change in creative. The starter pack is good for roughly 24 minutes of food and 21 minutes of water, which the Home tab's trip readout will tell you. {{survival-meters}} {{trip-preparation-readout}}

rows: Drink (+22 thirst) and refill every Empty flask you carry.
Drink one carried Water flask (+35 thirst); you keep the Empty flask.
Eat one food: Berries first, then Venison, Raw meat, and Cooked meat last.
Click a food in the Pack
Eat it. Click a Water flask to drink, the same as T. Within reach of water, that refills your empty flasks instead of drinking.

blocks.text: Only four foods exist. Berries come only from the starter pack, so renewable food comes from hunting and {{guide:fishing|fishing}}, best cooked over charcoal (below). Fruit blocks and Date clusters are building blocks, not food. {{eating}} {{drinking-flasks}}

T only reaches water that you can see from your chest. A solid block between you and the water stops the drink, and so does a block that the line only clips at a corner or edge. Remove the block or step to the open side.

Hold left click on a block within 6 m. A progress bar fills before the block breaks; a full one-metre block yields up to eight pieces. Each swing that lands while you mine gives a soft tap of the block's sound. Letting go or breaking the block makes no tap. Hold [[Shift]] to take a single half-metre piece of any block except a log or cactus. Logs and cactus fell the whole connected tree or stem instead, and Shift does not change that. Keep space in your pack and read the status line if gathering is refused. {{mining-harvesting}}

Your pack is limited by capacity, 1000, not by slots. {{carry-capacity}} Any block can be mined by hand; a tool only speeds up its own material: the pickaxe about 4× on rock, glass and masonry, the hatchet about 3.6× on logs, boards and leaves, the shovel about 3.4× on loose ground. {{mining-speed-tools}}

Press [[E]] and choose **Pack** to browse the icon grid. Hover an icon for its name, amount and help; click to use or equip it. [[Ctrl]]+[[F]] searches by item name, and the sort button switches between groups and alphabetical order. Hover an item and press [[1]]–[[9]] or [[0]], or drag it onto a hotbar slot, to bind that item kind. This makes a shortcut; it does not move or split the carried quantity. {{pack-items-list}} {{planned-inventory-overhaul}}

In survival, [[J]] drops one piece of the selected item; [[Ctrl]]+[[J]] drops everything of that kind. With Pack open, hover its icon first. After a short delay, approach the dropped stack to collect what fits; anything that does not fit stays on the ground. Dragging an item off the pack does not drop it, and dragging a hotbar slot off the bar only clears that shortcut. {{planned-ground-drops}}
Water and other liquids cannot be collected.

Your four starter board pieces can make a first Stone hatchet once you have four natural-stone pieces, such as Gravel. You can make that hatchet before felling a tree by hand; then gather logs and split more boards for your other tools.

items: Mine a log piece from a tree and open the inventory with [[E]], then the **Craft** tab.
Choose one of the 'Split … boards' recipes: one log piece makes four board pieces.
Mine stone blocks; any of the 26 natural stones counts.
Craft a Stone hatchet, Stone pickaxe or Stone shovel, then the sword if you want to hunt. Crafting a tool equips it automatically.

blocks.text: There is a single tool tier, and tools never wear out. There is no workbench: everything is crafted from the Craft tab. {{stone-tools}}

Choose the recipe you want on the **Craft** tab first. With the inventory closed, [[X]] repeats that recipe once. If materials are missing, it shows a message instead of making a different recipe. {{quick-craft-x}}

Animals never attack you. Left click one to hit it: a bare hand or ordinary tool deals 12 damage and the Stone sword deals 28. In survival, collect its dropped items by approaching them. If your pack is full, free some capacity and return for the remaining items. {{melee-attacks}} {{animal-drops}}

Cook from your pack anywhere on the Craft tab's **Fire & food** section, or on a placed cooking stove ({{guide:crafting-and-recipes|Crafting and recipes}}). There is no campfire or furnace. Raw meat restores 8 hunger and Cooked meat 30, and one Venison roasts into two Cooked meat. {{fire-and-glass-chain}} {{cooking-stove}}

items: Stand on dry, solid ground, open the **Home** tab and choose **Establish home**. It costs 8 board pieces in Survival and nothing in Creative, and places a small crate 1.5 m beside you.
Move items to and from the crate by clicking rows in the Home tab; it holds up to 400 capacity while you are within 6 m. Shift + click moves as many as fit.
Build a roof with cover on at least two sides next to the crate, then choose **Rest / set respawn** there.

rows: Move between the three buttons and the Pack and Home lists. Up from the first row returns to the buttons.
Turn the page of the selected list.
Use the selected button, or move one of the selected item. Hold [[Shift]] to move as many as fit.

blocks.text: If the crate is destroyed, stand within 6 m of its old spot and choose **Establish home** again to rebuild it for 8 board pieces (free in Creative). The old spot needs dry ground, solid ground under it and nobody standing in it. Otherwise the game refuses the repair and keeps your boards and stored items.

To move your home, empty its storage, stand within 6 m of the crate and choose **Pack up**. Survival gives back 8 Alder board pieces, so leave room for them in your pack; Creative gives nothing back. Your last rest point stays, and you can establish a new home elsewhere.

Resting sets your respawn point and refills stamina; it does not heal or feed you. Leaves and tree trunks count as cover, plants and water do not. Lying in a bed is separate: it never moves your respawn point. {{home-crate}} {{rest-respawn-point}}
Home on a server

On a server, only the world's saved owner has a Home crate. Anyone else is refused with 'This personal Home belongs to the saved world owner'. The first button reads **Establish / repair (8 boards)** in Survival or **Establish / repair (free)** in Creative, and **Repair crate** once your Home storage has opened. Storage, rest and Pack up follow the solo rules, and the crate must stand on a plot you may build on.
Each action shows '… | waiting for server' until the server confirms it, for example 'Rested at Home | respawn point set'. If it is refused, select the Home tab again to refresh it.

In Creative on a server, building or repairing the crate is free and Pack up gives no boards. When you join a Creative server, the list is headed **Carried supplies**: it shows only what you really carry on the server, so free catalogue items cannot be stored. As the Creative host, wait until your pack is confirmed; until then the tab says 'Home storage waits for pack confirmation'.

items: **Falls:** up to 3 m is free, each extra metre costs 5 HP, so about 23 m is fatal from full health. Only landing on solid ground counts. {{fall-damage-hazards}}
**Starvation and thirst** when the bars run empty.
**Explosions.** No drowning, lava, fire or hostile animals exist in this version. Direct fire/lava contact hazards remain planned.

**Death** opens a 'You died' screen showing the cause and respawn location. Click **Respawn** or press [[Enter]] when ready. You keep your inventory and return to your rest point, or a nearby safe spot if it is blocked or flooded. Until you rest at home, the rest point is the world's start. {{death-respawn}}

blocks.text: Base-game survival has no body-temperature meter or ambient-temperature damage. Rain, cold nights and altitude have no temperature penalty. Shelter still matters for resting. {{temperature-shelter}}

The game marks 15 first-time steps of a survival life. Each one counts once per world, only in survival mode, and the reached set is saved with the world. A milestone shows in the status line as 'Milestone: <name> (<reached>/15)'. Open the inventory with [[E]] and the **Milestones** tab to see all 15 and what reaches each one. Reached ones are marked with +; the rest show with -.

rows: Fell a tree by hand. Only a log counts, so cutting leaves or a stump does not.
Split logs into boards, for example with a Split boards recipe.
Craft any tool, such as a Stone hatchet.
Make a home at a storage crate (Establish home).
Cook a meal on the Craft tab (Cook raw meat or Roast venison). Cooking on a stove does not count.
Reach an expedition landmark on foot.

blocks.text: Creative mode reaches no milestones. The Milestones tab is read-only and cannot be used to claim one.

Planting and growing food, a placeable furnace with smelting and metal tools, and progression beyond the milestones remain planned. Follow their status in the {{planned-planting-food-plants|feature ledger}}.

guides.title: Crafting and recipes
guides.headline:
Crafting,
all 151 recipes.
guides.summary: How the Craft tab and its queue work, which ingredients can be mixed, cooking on a stove, and the complete recipe list with amounts.
guides.lead: No workbench, fire or furnace is needed: every recipe is crafted from the pack. This guide explains the panel and its short crafting queue, shows how to cook on a placed stove and lists every recipe with its exact amounts.

verification.method: The recipe tables are generated from data/recipes.json, refreshed on 8 November 2026 from the complete Craft-tab registry at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c and rechecked at 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480 (unchanged, with new source lines): 151 recipes, including the two cooking recipes shared with the stove and 90 doors by wood. tools/validate_guides.py --game rechecks every name, section, amount, game description and source line against that export. The Craft tab, its queue, the Ready filter, starred recipes and the X shortcut were source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480 (game/craft_queue.rs, game/crafting.rs, game/inventory_input.rs, game/inventory_qol.rs, game/net_client/crafting.rs, and the panel and screen drawing in voxelgame-render inventory_ui.rs and hud.rs). The cooking stove plan's description and connected tooltip were rechecked at 251b9e46 (inventory.rs:811, the renderer's inventory_ui.rs:391-400). The block-type section, the rest of the cooking stove, the fire and cooking text, the ingredient groups and the Glow crystal section were source-checked at dfeb362d. The gathering section keeps its earlier check (dd29d91). The Pack text in 'Gathering and reading the pack' was re-checked on 8 November 2026 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480: voxelgame-render inventory_ui.rs:318-331,367-414,453-560; voxelgame-core game/inventory_qol.rs:79-87, game/inventory_input.rs:292-327,395-401 and inventory.rs:1050-1075.
verification.limits: Source-checked at Voxelgame dfeb362d and 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested. The crafting queue and cooking on a server were not tried live. Amounts are carried pieces: 8 pieces make one full one-metre block. Furnaces, smelting and metal tools do not exist yet.

blocks.text: Open the inventory with [[E]] and choose **Craft**. Recipes are grouped into four sections: Timber, Fire & food, Materials and Tools & arms. Each ingredient shows as carried / required; in Survival a missing one reads 'Need … more'. The line below says 'Ready to craft', 'Gather the missing ingredients' or 'Free carry capacity for the output'. Every recipe is crafted anywhere, with no workbench, fire or furnace. {{crafting-panel}}

rows: Left / Right arrows, or click a section
Enter or C, or click Queue
Queue one batch. In Creative the button reads Create and the recipe is made at once.
Shift + Enter, Shift + C, Shift + click Queue, or click Review craft all

Count how many batches you can make now, at most 256. The button then reads 'Confirm all: … batches'. Press again, or click it, to queue them all as one order. If your pack changes first, you get a new count instead.
Cancel drops the review. Stop queue appears while orders wait and clears them all. Nothing unfinished is spent.
Show only recipes you can make now, including room in the pack for the result. Click again to show all.
Star or unstar the selected recipe. You can star up to four.
Starred recipes button, or a starred recipe's name
List your starred recipes from every section, or jump straight to one.

items: Ready recipes, Star and Starred recipes are the three small icon buttons under the section buttons. Hover one to see its name. Ready recipes and Starred recipes are highlighted while switched on. {{recipe-ready-filter}}

Each starred recipe also gets a button with its name under the icons. A fifth star is refused with 'Four favorites pinned; unstar one to make room'. Choosing a section leaves the starred list. {{starred-recipes}}
The Ready filter works on the starred list too. If nothing matches, the list says 'No recipes match these filters'.
Stars and the Ready filter last for this session only. They are not saved with the world.

blocks.text: The crafting queue

items: In Survival every craft is an order in a short queue. Queue says 'Queued … | materials kept until finished'. Each order takes 0.8 seconds, then the next one starts. {{craft-queue}}
The panel, and the screen during play, show 'Crafting (…) | recipe' with a progress bar. The number counts the orders in the queue, including the one being made.
Up to 8 orders fit. A ninth is refused with 'Craft queue full (8 orders) | finish or cancel in Craft'. A Confirm all order counts as one: all its batches finish together after 0.8 seconds.
Materials stay in your pack until an order finishes. If you cannot afford an order when you ask, nothing is queued and the status line says 'Cannot queue … | check materials and carry capacity'.

Queued orders do not set materials aside. If an earlier order or anything else uses them, or the result no longer fits, the order shows 'Waiting' and the status line says 'Craft waiting | restore materials or pack space, or cancel in Craft'. Nothing is spent until the whole order can finish.
Crafting carries on whether the inventory is open or closed. It stops while the pause menu, the settings or the fullscreen map is open, and continues afterwards.
Stop queue clears every order and says 'Craft queue cancelled | all unspent materials kept'.
Queued orders are not saved. After you reload the world the queue is empty and the unspent materials are still in your pack. Switching to Creative also empties the queue.
In Creative there is no queue. The ingredients are free, but the result still needs room in the pack ('Not enough free carry capacity').
A crafted tool is equipped at once and a crafted boat is selected.
You cannot open the inventory while inside a vehicle.

blocks.text: Crafting on a server

items: Crafting works only in Survival ('Crafting on servers requires Survival mode').
Each order still takes 0.8 seconds. Then the status line says 'Requesting … | awaiting server', and the next order waits for the server's answer.
A refusal reads 'Crafting refused: … | materials kept'. Stop queue cannot recall an order that was already sent: 'Queued crafts cancelled | submitted craft still awaits server'.
While crafts are queued, chests, Home storage and furniture storage wait for them, for example 'Chest waiting for the current server action | items kept'.

blocks.text: Counts are half-metre pieces. One full one-metre block is 8 pieces, so a recipe that needs 8 of a material needs one block of it.
A few ingredients accept a whole group of materials, and you can mix the members freely. {{ingredient-groups}}

items: **Boards:** any of the 15 board species, mixed freely. Doors by wood are the exception: they need boards of exactly their wood.
**Natural stone:** any of 26 natural stones.
**Plant fiber or Wool.**

blocks.text: Every log has its own splitting recipe, so there is no shared hardwood group. Each makes boards of its own species; Deadwood makes Alder boards.

Every other ingredient must be that exact material: Sand (not other sands), Clay (not ochre, umber, sienna, cracked or banded clay), Reeds (not Tall reeds), Limestone, Granite, Cobblestone, Moss, Chalk, Basalt, Red rock, Marble, White plaster, Wildflowers, Paper screen, Glass, Charcoal, Feather, Raw meat, Venison and TNT.

Not usable as natural stone: Magma stone, Iron ore, Bog iron, Amethyst, Salt, Sulfur crust, Mineral crust, Geyser stone and any crafted masonry. Sandstone is the exception: it counts as natural stone, although you can also craft it from sand.

Select a recipe on the **Craft** tab first. Then, with the inventory closed, each press of [[X]] queues one more batch of that recipe in the same 0.8-second queue. It works on foot in Survival. {{quick-craft-x}}

items: If the selected recipe lacks materials, nothing is queued and the status line says 'Missing materials for … | pick another recipe on the Craft tab'. X never switches to a different recipe.
In Creative, X only says 'Crafting uses carried resources in survival'.
X does nothing while you are in a vehicle. Its key binding is called **Craft selected recipe** in Settings > Controls > Key bindings.

blocks.text: Fire work is Craft-tab crafting, not a placed furnace: burn 4 boards into 2 Charcoal, then spend Charcoal to cook meat, fire Sand into Glass, blow Glass into flasks, and fire clay, limestone and lacquer. Fill flasks by pressing [[T]] at water. You can also cook meat on a placed cooking stove (next section). {{fire-and-glass-chain}}
Besides the 'Fire glass' recipe, the Survey workshop landmark's one-time find gives 8 Glass.

A placed **Cooking stove** cooks Raw meat or Venison with Charcoal. It uses the same two recipes as the Craft tab: one Raw meat and one Charcoal make one Cooked meat, and one Venison and one Charcoal make two. Each batch takes 0.8 seconds. {{cooking-stove}}

items: Open [[E]] > **Build** and click the **Stove** plan. In Survival the Build tab appears only while you carry a **Furniture hammer**; in Creative it is always there.
Choose **Feet** (a board wood) and **Body** (**Stone** or **Iron**). In Survival, placing the stove spends one board of that wood and six Stone or six Iron ore pieces. Creative placement is free.
Aim at the top of solid ground, press [[R]] to turn the ghost and right-click to place it. The stove is one metre square and one metre high.
Press [[B]] to put the plan away and select an ordinary block or empty hands. Then right-click the stove from within 6 m. The inventory opens on its **Cooking stove** tab.

rows: Add raw meat, Add venison, Add charcoal
Move one from your pack into the stove. Shift + click moves as many as fit.
Cook one raw piece. That piece and one Charcoal stay reserved until the batch finishes.
Stop the batch. Nothing is spent; the food and Charcoal stay in the stove.
Move finished Cooked meat into your pack. It needs free pack capacity.
Move food or Charcoal that is not reserved back into your pack.

items: The stove holds up to 16 raw pieces, 16 Charcoal and 32 Cooked meat. It takes one kind of raw food at a time: take out the meat before adding venison, or the other way round.
Start cooks one batch only. Press it again for the next one; the stove never starts another batch by itself.
Start can refuse with 'Add raw food before cooking', 'Add charcoal before cooking' or 'Take out cooked food to make room for the complete recipe'.
Creative uses real carried food and Charcoal too. The stove never makes free Cooked meat.
A batch keeps cooking while the panel is closed or you walk away. It stops while the pause menu, the settings or the fullscreen map is open, or while you are dead, and continues afterwards.
Saving keeps the contents and the time left. Nothing cooks while the world is closed.

Moving or turning the stove keeps its contents. Empty it completely before taking it up, or you see 'Empty the cooking stove before removing it'. Furniture controls are in {{guide:building-basics|Building basics}}.

blocks.text: The stove only cooks meat. It has no flame, gives off no heat, does not hurt you and does not set nearby wood alight. It is not a furnace and cannot smelt or fire glass, bricks or plaster.
Cooking on a server

Cooking also works when you join a server or LAN world and when you host your own world. Right-click the stove as usual. The tab first says it is waiting for the server, and after each click the buttons wait until the server confirms your pack. If the stove hint says 'Cooking waits for the server world, stock and recovery state', wait a moment and try again. Other players can use the same stove, plot claims still apply, and the server keeps cooking a started batch after you leave.
Cooking on a stove does not count for the **Hot meal** milestone. In Survival, craft Cook raw meat or Roast venison once on the Craft tab to reach it.

Cutting a log on a natural tree, or a cactus stem, brings down that piece and everything growing from it. Cut the bottom log to take the whole tree. Cut a branch and the trunk below it stays standing. {{tree-felling}}

items: In survival the chop takes as long as all the wood and leaves it removes together. All of it goes into your pack.
If the whole harvest does not fit, the status line says 'Need X capacity free to collect this connected tree' and nothing is cut.
A log you placed yourself breaks like any other block, one piece at a time.
A finished tree reports 'Felled a tree' with the number of logs and leaves.

blocks.text: Shores mix Clay (below sea level), Gravel and Sand. Desert ground is Sand. Reeds grow in wetlands. Wild flax grows in some meadows of worlds made with the current generator. Feathers, wool and meat come from animals. {{material-sources}}
Older worlds have no Wild flax, so use Wool for bindings there.

Open **E > Pack** to see what you carry as a grid of icons. Tools come first, then food and drink, blocks, materials and spawn eggs, each group sorted by name; the sort button switches to one alphabetical list. [[Ctrl]]+[[F]] searches by name. {{pack-items-list}}

rows: Use it, select it or equip it. A material with no use says it is stored as a crafting resource.
Hover an item, then press 1-9 or 0
Bind it to that hotbar slot.
Drag an item onto a hotbar slot
Bind it to that slot while the inventory is open.
Mouse wheel, or the Previous / Next buttons
Switch between the item grid and a turning character portrait.

blocks.text: Hover an item for its name, amount, category, a short description and click hints; in Pack the tooltip also says how to get it and how much capacity one piece takes. The side panel shows the item, its short description and what it is used for. {{item-info-previews}}
'USED IN' shows only the first recipe that names the exact item. Some stones count through the natural-stone group, so their panel can say 'USE: PLACE / BUILD' even when a recipe accepts them.
At Voxelgame dfeb362d the Blocks reference lists 285 block types besides Air. Each has its own name and colour. Recipes on this page name the blocks they use. {{block-materials-catalogue}}

items: Six block types are water: Water, Hot spring water, Dark fjord water, Fresh water, Black water and Boiling water.
Iron ore and Bog iron can be mined and placed. No Craft-tab recipe uses them, and the game has no smelting yet. Iron ore can pay for the iron body of furniture such as the cooking stove.
Glow crystal is a glowing decorative block. No recipe uses it, and the world does not generate it naturally. The Stone overlook landmark usually has one piece.

blocks.text: Every recipe in this version, in the order the Craft tab shows them. Each makes the stated amount from the stated inputs in one craft. The 90 doors by wood come last in the Timber section, after the Small sailing boat, and have their own table here.

When a door recipe is selected, its **Style**, **Wood** and **Size** buttons jump to another door recipe. Style cycles Plain, Panelled and Windowed; Wood cycles the 15 woods and, for a plain door, **Any boards**; Size switches between 1 x 2 m and 2 x 3 m. Choose a wood before changing the style of an Any boards door.

Red lantern, Alder rifle, Four rifle rounds, TNT and Two dynamite sticks use only materials you can gather or craft: stone, sand, reeds, boards, Paper screen and Charcoal. No recipe uses Glow crystal. {{lumen-crystal-supply}}
A placeable furnace or campfire, smelting, metal tools and tool durability are planned and not in this version. The cooking stove only cooks meat.

guides.title: Install, update and find your worlds
guides.headline:
Install the game,
keep your worlds.
guides.summary: Install Voxelgame, use Linux managed update and rollback, and preserve your worlds and preferences.
guides.lead: Each installer builds the game from source and adds a launcher. Player worlds, editable data and shared preferences live outside the versioned application payloads; updates preserve them.

verification.method: Update/world-configuration follow-up at 36ff7d46073a7f8d0202a1b47b6d7deb580f301b. Linux orchestration passed 30 isolated tests; a compiled native binary passed first-install/reinstall, live headless-session preservation, version reporting and rollback. Save/startup regressions and inspected headless captures cover compatibility and switching; other guide details retain the earlier audit. Targeted world-library follow-up at aa136e0103ce5599c6d8a9f70c669dbc758b7357: source-checked Create options, selected-world actions, remembered local world and backup paths. Installation/update acceptance above keeps its earlier check. On 8 November 2026 the macOS and Windows update scripts, Create world keys and world deletion were re-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480: README.md:21-25; START-HERE-macOS.txt:6-9; docs/UPDATING.md:16-92; Update-macOS.command, update-windows.cmd and scripts/desktop/update_github.py:42-72; game/startup_create.rs:94-196 and game/startup/worlds.rs:420-495 (beneath crates/voxelgame-core/src/); voxelgame-render startup_ui.rs:200-270 and startup_ui/worlds.rs:366-436; src/worlds.rs:575-623.
verification.limits: Not fully play-tested. Official-source fetch/build is covered by isolated Git/fake-compiler tests, not a second native rebuild. Windows/macOS managed parity and native validation are pending. Rollback cannot undo newer save formats. No new native install, world-switch, backup or LAN test was run for the 5 November follow-up. The 8 November update-script, Create world and deletion text was source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested.

blocks.text: You need an internet connection, several GB of free disk space and a working Vulkan graphics driver. On Linux the game runs in an X11 or XWayland session; it has no native Wayland window.
Keep the extracted source folder until setup finishes. You can delete it afterwards.

items: Open a terminal in the extracted source folder.
Run **bash install.sh** as your normal user. Do not use sudo; setup only uses it for system packages.

Read the plan and confirm it. First setup installs compiler/audio tools and Rust, builds the game and adds a launcher. Existing Linux installations reuse their tools without administrator prompts; repair missing prerequisites separately.
Start Voxelgame from the application menu.

rows: Install the app into another folder
Skip the tool install; use this on other distributions after installing the tools yourself (see docs/INSTALLING.md)

blocks.text: Setup never starts the game and never touches existing worlds.
The Windows installer has not been tested on a real Windows PC yet.

items: Double-click **install-windows.cmd**.
Confirm the plan. If Windows asks, approve the Microsoft C++ Build Tools installer.
Wait while setup downloads any missing Build Tools, Rust and FFmpeg, then builds the game.
Start Voxelgame from the Start menu. The shortcut has no Voxelgame icon.

blocks.text: If the compiler setup asks you to restart Windows, restart it and run the installer again. Managed PCs may need an administrator to allow PowerShell scripts. In PowerShell, run **install-windows.ps1** with the same options as the Linux installer: -Yes or -Prefix PATH.
The macOS build is not validated yet. Graphics and sound are untested, and the game may fail to start on some Macs.

items: Double-click **Install-macOS.command** and press Return to accept the plan.
If Apple offers the Command Line Tools installer, finish it.
If Homebrew asks for your password, enter your Mac password.
Open Voxelgame.app from the Applications folder in your home folder.

blocks.text: The app is unsigned and not notarized. If macOS blocks it, open System Settings > Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway. You can also run **bash install.sh** in Terminal. Do not turn off Gatekeeper.
On some Macs the F4 mode key needs Fn+F4.

Linux managed installs can report their version, update from official source and select the previous verified installation. macOS and Windows have update scripts that rebuild the official source, but no version report or rollback yet.

items: Save your world and close the game when convenient. Updating does not restart a running session; reopen afterwards to use the new release.

From a clean official Git checkout, run **bash install.sh --version**, then **bash install.sh --update**. After archive setup, use **~/.local/share/voxelgame/app/launch.sh --version** and **--update** instead. For a custom installation, use its launch.sh or the source script with **--prefix PATH**.

Read the installed and available commit, build progress and final result. Linux needs Python 3.9+, Git, a prepared Rust/compiler toolchain and at least 5 GiB free. The update command does not install prerequisites or ask for administrator access.
Worlds, settings, screenshots and editable projects remain in their separate data folders.
Updates build official source in isolation and verify the completed files before switching the launcher. Dirty source checkouts cause a refusal; nothing is stashed or reset.
If fetching, building or verification fails, keep using the old launcher. Fix the reported network, disk-space or permission problem and retry.
Run **bash install.sh --rollback** to verify and select the previous release. Old releases are retained; updates do not delete them automatically.
Logs are under ~/.local/state/voxelgame/update-*.log unless the log folder was overridden.

blocks.text: Keep backups. Rollback switches application files only. An older executable may refuse worlds saved in a newer format; rollback does not undo changes to worlds or settings. Linux headless session preservation was checked; Windows and macOS updates have not been run on a real machine yet.

On macOS, close the game, extract a fresh complete source folder and double-click **Update-macOS.command** (or run **bash update.sh**). On Windows, close the game and double-click **update-windows.cmd** in a complete source folder. Both rebuild official `main` with the Git, Python 3.9+, Rust and compiler tools you already have, and need at least 5 GiB free. They keep your worlds and settings and the previous application files, and never install missing tools or ask for administrator access. They have no **--version** or **--rollback**; verified rollback is Linux only.

rows: Worlds and editable data: ~/.local/share/voxelgame/data. Installer logs: ~/.local/state/voxelgame
Worlds and editable data: ~/Library/Application Support/Voxelgame. Installer logs: ~/Library/Logs/Voxelgame
Worlds and editable data: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Voxelgame\data. Installer logs: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Voxelgame\logs

blocks.text: On Linux, shared display, audio, controls and accessibility preferences are in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/voxelgame/settings, defaulting to ~/.config/voxelgame/settings. Mode, environment controls and progression remain in the world file. Other platforms have not received native profile-location acceptance.

Setup writes a log once it starts, including runs that fail later. It prints the log path at the start, and a failed run does not repeat it. A stop before setup starts, such as a cancelled plan, leaves no log. Its file name is install-<date>-<id>.log. On Linux and macOS, set VOXELGAME_INSTALL_LOG_DIR to change the log folder.

items: Open **Worlds** and choose **Create world**. Enter a name, or leave it blank for a default name.
Leave **Seed** blank for a fresh world, or enter a non-negative whole number. Choose Creative or Survival and a terrain generation; the default is generation 12.

Use [[Tab]] or the Up/Down arrows to move between fields; Left/Right (or Space) change Mode and Terrain generation. Choose **Create world** or press [[Enter]] to confirm, or **Cancel** / [[Esc]] to return without creating it.

blocks.text: To reopen a world, select its row and choose **Play world**, press [[Enter]], or double-click the row. Typing filters names; the mouse wheel, arrows and Page Up / Page Down browse the list. Worlds shows the selected save’s seed, mode and generation when those details can be read. {{worlds-page}} {{world-seed-selection}}

Use **Rename** ([[Ctrl]]+[[R]]) to change its display name, or **Duplicate** ([[Ctrl]]+[[D]]) to make a separately named playable copy. Rename keeps the save’s path. Duplicate saves the active local world first; stop hosting before duplicating it.

To delete a world, select it and hold **Delete world** (or the [[Delete]] key) for 3 seconds; letting go early cancels. Deleting removes the save, its name, preview and star for good. Backups you made are kept, so choose **Create backup** first if you might want the world back. The world you are currently in cannot be deleted: load another world first.

items: Each world has a .vxw save in the worlds folder inside the data folder, plus separate name, preview and session-history files when present.

A named new world uses a lowercase folder such as worlds/my-island/world.vxw. If that folder exists, a number is added. An empty name or a name with no usable letters or numbers gets world-0001, world-0002 and so on.
Stars live separately in worlds/favourites.txt. The last selected local world is recorded in worlds/last-world.txt.

blocks.text: Continue resumes your last local world

After a restart, Continue resumes the last successfully selected local save. If that record is missing or its file is gone, the fallback path is worlds/debug/debug.vxw. On a fresh installation with no saved world, Continue is disabled: choose Worlds to create one. An unreadable save opens a recovery dialog and is kept intact. {{startup-active-world}}

World mode, generator, time/weather/season controls and progression belong to that world. Display, audio, controls and accessibility preferences are shared across worlds. Untouched terrain is regenerated from the saved seed and generation.

Choose **Create backup** ([[Ctrl]]+[[B]]) for the selected world. The active local world is saved first; stop hosting before backing it up. The result names a completed snapshot under the data folder’s backups folder. Read {{world-backups}} for copying a snapshot back into Worlds.

The installer does not move worlds from a source checkout started with ./run.sh. Copying that worlds folder into the data folder with the game closed is inferred from the save paths and has not been tested in this wiki.

Linux with a Vulkan graphics driver and an X11 or XWayland session is the tested platform. The Windows (64-bit Intel or AMD, Windows 10 or 11) and macOS (Apple Silicon, or Intel with a Metal GPU) installers are included, but no real machine has checked graphics and sound on them yet. {{system-requirements}}
The first build needs internet access and several GB of free disk space. The README's 60 FPS target assumes at least an integrated GPU. Software Vulkan (llvmpipe) is only for diagnostics.
There is no uninstaller. Delete the app folder and its launcher by hand. {{uninstall}}

items: **Linux:** delete the app folder, `~/.local/share/voxelgame/app` by default, and `~/.local/share/applications/voxelgame.desktop`.
**macOS:** delete `~/Applications/Voxelgame.app`.
**Windows:** delete the app folder and the Voxelgame shortcut in your Start menu Programs folder. The FFmpeg copy in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Voxelgame\tools` stays unless you delete it too.
Compilers, Rust, Homebrew and audio tools that setup installed stay on the PC.

blocks.text: Your worlds stay in the data folder until you delete it. Deleting the data folder removes all worlds for good, so copy any world you want to keep first.
Developers can build the game without the installer. With Rust 1.75 or newer and the Linux packages installed, run `cargo run --release --locked --bin voxelgame`, or `./run.sh`. {{build-from-source}}

items: `run.sh` rebuilds only when sources, assets or Cargo files are newer than the program. It shows a small Preparing the game window while it builds.
Started this way, worlds live in the worlds folder inside the source folder.

guides.title: Fixing startup, sound and save problems
guides.headline:
Fix startup,
sound and saves.
guides.summary: Find the error message, check your graphics driver and sound players, and recover a world that will not load.
guides.lead: Most startup failures print their reason to a terminal. Start the game from a terminal first, then use the matching section below.

Windows and macOS graphics and sound are marked Limited because no real machine has validated them yet. These targeted save corrections are source checks only; no new play test was run. blocks.text: When the game cannot start, or stops on a fatal error, it closes and prints a report that begins **qiqi could not continue**; its **Error:** (or **Panic:**) line gives the reason. The report is also saved as a details.txt file, and its last line, **Diagnostic file:**, says where. On Linux, a launch without options, such as from the application menu, also opens a **qiqi could not continue** window with **Copy details** and **Close**; it needs Python 3 and GTK 3. {{native-error-window}} Windows and macOS show no window yet, so start the game from a terminal there to read the report.

items: A mistyped command-line option makes the game exit with code 2.
Any other failure makes it exit with code 1.

blocks.text: Messages you may see:

items: **no Vulkan-compatible graphics adapter found**: the graphics driver is missing. See Graphics driver problems below.
**GPU ran out of memory during startup**: lower **Settings > Graphics > Display > Horizon distance**, then try again.
**Nearby terrain took too long to prepare; please try again**: shown on the main menu. Try again, or lower **Settings > Graphics > Display > Horizon distance**.
**audio disabled: playback command unavailable**: sound players are missing. See Sound and music below.

blocks.text: Setup failures are written to an installer log. See {{guide:install-and-worlds|Install, update and find your worlds}}.
Problems with other worlds appear on the main menu instead of closing the game.

If a world cannot be read, the game shows **World could not be loaded** with the file and the reason, and keeps your save. Choose **Back to menu** to pick another world, or **Open worlds folder** to find the file. Keep its `.vxw` file, and copy it somewhere safe before trying repairs or a different game version.
Continue normally resumes the last selected local world. If that world will not open, use the error message to identify the affected file rather than assuming it is the default world.
See {{guide:saves|Saves and world files}} for loading limits and backups, and {{guide:install-and-worlds|Install, update and find your worlds}} for the data folder.
Press **F6** to save a local world. If a save or stopped-host recovery fails, keep the game open and read the reported error before retrying or leaving.
For autosave, backups and the stopped-host recovery choices, follow {{guide:saves|Saves and world files}}. Opening Main menu while hosting does not stop the host.
A crash can lose unsaved progress. Keep a separate backup of a world you want to protect.
Voxelgame needs a working Vulkan graphics driver. On Linux it runs in an X11 or XWayland session. It has no native Wayland window.

items: **Debian and Fedora**: the installer adds Mesa Vulkan drivers.
**Arch**: install **vulkan-intel** or **vulkan-radeon**, or your NVIDIA driver.
**macOS**: a Metal-capable GPU is required.

blocks.text: The game picks your high-performance GPU first. If that fails, it falls back to a software renderer such as llvmpipe. The fallback is useful for diagnosis but too slow for normal play.

To reduce GPU load, try **Settings > Graphics > Display > Graphics preset > Low**, or set **Horizon distance** lower, turn off **Settings > Advanced > Diagnostics > Distant terrain**, or set **Shader** to **None** (Graphics > Display).
Windows graphics have not been validated on a real Windows PC yet.
Sound effects need a player program: **aplay** from alsa-utils on Linux, or **ffplay** on Windows and macOS. The installers set these up. Without a player the game runs silently.
Music also needs **ffmpeg** to decode the songs. Song files may be mp3, ogg, wav or flac.

items: If ffmpeg is missing, Music turns itself off and the status line shows **Music unavailable: ...**.
After you install ffmpeg, open **Settings > Audio** and switch Music back on.

sections.title: Record lag spikes for a bug report

blocks.text: With the Performance overlay (F3) on, a frame that takes at least 25 ms and more than twice your frame budget is written to a log. Turn F3 off to stop recording. {{lag-spike-log}}

items: **Linux:** `~/.local/state/voxelgame/lag-spikes.jsonl`, or inside `$XDG_STATE_HOME/voxelgame` if that variable is set.
Each entry has the world seed, your position, the frame cost and up to eight of the slowest causes.

blocks.text: The F3 panel shows the log status: armed, recording, dropped or unavailable. Attach the file when you report a slow frame.

guides.title: Hunting, weapons and animals
guides.headline:
Hunt with a sword,
bow, rifle or rock.
guides.summary: Animals never attack. Learn the melee, throwing, bow and rifle controls, and what each kill gives you.
guides.lead: Hunting is one of the two renewable food sources in survival; the other is fishing. No animal fights back, so the only hard part is getting close enough and keeping the weapon ready.

verification.method: Controls, damage, draw times and drop rules come from the game source at the audited commit. Each ledger entry lists its source lines. The cooking advice in 'What you get from a kill' was re-checked at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c on 8 November 2026. The drop rules in that section were re-checked on 8 November 2026 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480: game/creature_melee.rs:38-81, game.rs:2121-2270, entities/melee.rs:10-11,194-286, game/item_drops.rs:102-137, dropped_items.rs:9-25 and entities/species_profile.rs:401-486, beneath crates/voxelgame-core/src/.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested in this guide. Draw, wind-up and reload times are the code values; check them in play if they feel different. The 8 November dfeb362d check covers only that cooking advice and was not play-tested. The drop rules were source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested.

blocks.text: Every animal is passive. None of them attack, chase or damage you. Farm animals stay calm near you. Small wild animals, such as rabbits and foxes, keep their distance and run when you come close. Any animal runs for a few seconds after you hurt it. {{no-hostile-mobs}} {{animal-behaviour}}
There is no taming, riding, breeding, feeding, milking or shearing.

sections.title: Hit with a hand, tool or sword

items: Get within reach of the animal and aim at it.
Left-click to hit it.
A hurt animal runs off for a few seconds. Chase it and hit it again.

blocks.text: A bare hand or an ordinary tool deals 12 damage. The Stone sword deals 28. In creative, one hit removes the animal and gives you nothing. Tall grass or flowers between you and the animal can block the hit. {{melee-attacks}}

rows: Wind up. A full wind-up takes 0.7 s.
Throw. A wind-up that is too short is cancelled.

blocks.text: Harder throws fly farther and hit harder. Each throw uses one rock in survival. A throw that cannot fly, such as one with no valid aim, keeps the rock. Rocks hurt animals only, not you or vehicles. {{throwing-rocks}}

items: Craft an Alder bow and some arrows.
Equip the bow. Press [[Tab]] or [[Shift]] + [[Tab]] to cycle through what you carry.
Hold right click to draw. A full draw takes 0.85 s.
Release to shoot. Letting go before about a fifth of a draw cancels the shot.

blocks.text: Longer draws fly faster and hit harder. In survival each shot uses one arrow, and arrows are not recovered. A shot that cannot fly, such as one with no valid aim, keeps the arrow. Arrows stop on grass, flowers and other small plants. An arrow that lands in grass or leaves makes a soft rustle. Other impacts make a thunk that fades out by about 48 m. Creative arrows are unlimited. {{alder-bow}}
The reed versions use reeds instead of wool or plant fiber for the string and shafts, so you do not need animal drops for them.

rows: Raise the sights for less spread and sway. You cannot aim while it reloads.
Does not reload the rifle. In survival, R eats food instead.

blocks.text: The rifle reloads itself about one second after every shot. Survival uses one rifle round per shot; creative is unlimited. A shot that cannot fly keeps its round. Rounds hurt animals and vehicles. {{alder-rifle}}

sections.title: What you get from a kill

blocks.text: In survival, a killed animal leaves its drops on the ground where it fell. After about a second, walk up to them to pick up what fits in your pack; anything that does not fit stays on the ground until you make room. Meat and venison are food, feathers make arrows, and wool can replace plant fiber. Hide has no use yet. Creative kills give nothing. {{animal-drops}}

Cook meat with Charcoal before you eat it: craft it on the Craft tab, or cook it on a placed {{cooking-stove|cooking stove}}. Cooked meat restores much more hunger than raw meat. See {{guide:first-survival-day|Your first survival day}} for the hunger numbers.

guides.title: Seasons and the look of the world
guides.headline:
Seasons change
how the world looks.
guides.summary: A year lasts 80 minutes. Each season changes colours and light. Blocks, building and tools stay the same. Snow and thinner leaves are planned, not in the game yet.
guides.lead: The season changes how the world looks, with no survival penalties. Nothing you build, mine or walk on changes with it.

verification.method: Re-checked against the game source at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026: year and season length, the starting season, season order and names (environment.rs), seasonal colour palettes (shader.wgsl), seasonal sky and sunlight (sky_light.rs), autumn falling leaves (game.rs, particles/ambient.rs), the Gameplay > World Season row (settings.rs, ui.rs, music_settings.rs), Home rest shelter (home.rs), and the absence of temperature effects (survival.rs, environment.rs) and of season checks in world content, animals and crafting.
verification.limits: Source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested. Season colours are described in words because no season screenshots exist yet.

blocks.text: A full year lasts 80 real minutes, so each season lasts 20 minutes. New worlds start in the middle of summer. The order is spring, summer, autumn and winter, then back to spring. {{seasons}}

Each season changes the colours of grass, broadleaf leaves, needles, blossoms and water, blending slowly from one season to the next. The sky and sunlight change too: autumn turns leaves and grass russet and gold, and winter mutes them to grey-green under a cooler, weaker light.

In autumn, single leaves drift down from broadleaf and blossom trees around you and blow with the wind. They are only for show: the trees keep all their blocks. Falling leaves need **Graphics > Display > Shader** set to Fast or Cinematic and **Interface > Accessibility > Reduce motion** off.

items: Press [[Esc]], choose **Settings**, then open **Gameplay > World**.
On the **Season** row, click **<** or **>** to hold Spring, Summer, Autumn or Winter. A held season shows its full colours.
Choose Auto to go back to the normal cycle. It carries on from the season you held.

blocks.text: While the cycle runs, the Season row reads **Auto /** and the current season, for example **Auto / summer**. A held season shows just its name. In survival you cannot change the row: the game says **Time, weather, and season controls are read-only in survival**. {{creative-world-controls}}
Base-game survival has no body-temperature meter or ambient-temperature damage. Seasons, time of day, rain and altitude do not cause cold or heat penalties. {{temperature-shelter}}
To rest at your Home crate and set your respawn point, you still need dry ground, a roof and cover on two sides. Shelter has no warmth effect.
The Home tab has no temperature line. Use its food, water, empty-flask, free-capacity and shelter readouts to prepare for a trip.

sections.title: What the season does not change

items: No snow falls and no snow blocks appear. Water does not freeze in winter.
Trees keep all their blocks. Leaves do not thin out; falling autumn leaves are only for show.
Weather follows its own pattern, not the season.
The season does not change which animals appear or what crafting needs.

sections.title: Planned, not in the game yet

blocks.text: Planned: leaves that thin out on some trees, and grass that looks snowy in winter. Until these ship, the game works as described above.

guides.title: Maps and finding your way back
guides.headline:
Mark it, find it,
get back to it.
guides.summary: Use the compact and fullscreen maps, the HUD compass, the biome locator, Journal places and destinations. Keep a build easy to find after a long trip.
guides.lead: Two maps show the generated terrain. You can mark places, set a destination and search for biomes. Your own builds are not drawn on the maps, so save a place before you travel far.

verification.method: Source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480 on 8 November 2026. Map keys: game.rs:1385-1428. blocks.text: The compact map is a small north-up view in the top-right corner. It shows 128 m across, centred on you, and is on by default. The fullscreen map is 512 m across when it opens and zooms from 128 m to about 131 km. {{compact-map}} {{fullscreen-map}}

rows: Show or hide the compact map.
Open or close the fullscreen map. The compact map stays.
Close it and hide the compact map.

blocks.text: To make the compact map turn with you, set **Settings > Interface > Layout > Compact map heading** to On. The way you face is then always at the top, and the N, E, S and W labels move round the edge. The fullscreen map always stays north-up.
The maps show generated terrain only. Blocks you place or dig do not appear on them. The compact map is hidden while a panel is open and in clean view ([[F1]]).

items: Press [[Shift]] + [[M]] to open the map. It opens centred on you. When you play offline, the world pauses while it is open. On a server, the world keeps running.
Scroll the mouse wheel over the map to zoom in or out.
Drag with the left mouse button to look around. Dragging does not move you.
Press **BACK TO PLAYER** in the side panel to centre the map on you again.

blocks.text: The readout under the map shows the X and Z position under the cursor and its distance from you. With the cursor off the map, it shows the map centre and your height. {{map-player-marker}} You are the grey arrow with a dark outline. It points the way you face.
N, E, S and W labels mark the edges. A scale bar sits in the lower-left corner, and a legend in the lower-right corner names the markers.

items: Open the fullscreen map.
Right-click the spot you want. The game adds a pin named Marker 1, Marker 2 and so on, and sets it as your destination. On water, the pin stands on the surface.
Right-click an existing pin to remove it.

blocks.text: Markers use the same 16-place limit as the Journal. Rename them in the Journal to give them a clear name. Pins show as small amber squares on both maps, with their names on the fullscreen map. {{map-right-click-markers}}

Right-clicking a pin removes it, even a named Journal place. To undo, open the Journal and press **Restore removed**. Only the last place you removed can come back, and only until you leave the world. If the game says the Journal is full, remove a place first.

items: Press [[E]], then click the **Journal** tab or press [[Tab]] until it shows. You can also click the **Journal** button on the fullscreen map.
Click the **Name** or **Note** field and type. Press [[Enter]] to finish typing. A name holds up to 32 plain letters and a note up to 96; accented and non-Latin letters take more room.
Click **Pin this location** to save the spot where you stand. It also becomes your destination. A blank name becomes Place 1, Place 2 and so on.
Click a place to select it. This also makes it your destination and loads its name and note. Edit them and click **Save selected note**.

blocks.text: The Journal holds 16 places and lists each one with its distance from you. Use **Prev** and **Next** to page through them. Places are saved per world. {{journal-places}}

items: **Remove selected pin** deletes the selected place.
**Restore removed** brings back the last place you removed, with its name and note.
**Show on map** opens the fullscreen map centred on the selected place, or on your home crate when no place is selected.

blocks.text: The destination is the place the maps and the screen point to. It can be a map marker, a Journal place or an expedition site. It is saved with the world. {{destination-beacon}}

items: On both maps it shows as an amber square with a +. When it is off the map, the square waits at the edge in its direction.
In the world it shows as an amber light column 320 m tall.
On screen it shows as a gold diamond with the name and distance. The diamond sticks to the screen edge when the place is out of view. It reads HERE within 3 m.
The Journal shows the distance to it under its buttons, for example To Camp: 120 m.

blocks.text: There is no clear button. Pick another place to change the destination, or remove the selected place to clear it, but only when that place is the destination. Removing another place keeps the destination. With no destination, the maps show your home crate as the + square instead, with no beacon or diamond. {{home-crate}}

items: Open the fullscreen map and click the search field on the left.
Type a name, such as crystal, meteorite, caldera or lava tunnel. The list filters as you type.
Press [[Enter]], or click a result. The map centres on the first match, highlights the matching terrain in cyan and drops a pin with the distance and coordinates.
Press **FIND NEXT** to search outward for another match at least about 1 km from the last one, or **CLEAR** to remove the pin and highlight.

blocks.text: The locator does not move you. Pan the map first if you want to search from another spot, because the search starts at the map centre. It only searches while the fullscreen map is open, out to about 131 km. NO MATCH IN SAMPLED AREA means it found nothing. {{map-locator}}
The list includes Volcano, Cliff island, Mountain range and all 92 biomes. A name marked * cannot appear in this world, because the world was made by an older version of the game.
In Creative you can jump to a place from the map. In Survival the map is a chart only.

items: Click a spot on the fullscreen map without dragging. You land on clear dry ground within about 9 m of it, or on the water surface when there is none.
Or click the **COORDINATES (METRES)** field, type X Z, or X Y Z for an exact height, and press [[Enter]] or **TELEPORT**. Spaces or commas both work, and values must be within ±1,000,000.

blocks.text: X Z always looks for a safe surface spot. An X Y Z spot must be free, or the game says Position blocked; try X Z instead. After the jump, the status line gives your new X, Y and Z and the biome. On a server, the server makes the jump and allows one trip a second.
Teleporting does not save where you came from, and there is no go back button. Save a Journal place before you jump. Leave the boat helm first. {{map-click-travel}} {{map-coordinate-teleport}}

In Survival, clicking the map only shows a reminder, and the button reads CREATIVE MODE ONLY. Zooming, dragging, the locator and markers still work, and the maps show the whole world, even places you have not visited. In a solo world, [[F4]] switches to Creative. {{survival-map-chart}}

The small readout under the compact map shows FPS, your X, Y and Z in metres and your biome. It is on each time you start the game. Turn it off in **Settings > Advanced > Diagnostics > FPS and coordinates**. It is hidden while a panel is open. {{position-readout}}

items: North is -Z and east is +X, so walking north makes Z smaller.
Write the numbers down before a long trip. They are the same numbers the coordinates field uses.

blocks.text: The HUD compass is off by default. Turn it on in **Settings > Interface > Layout > HUD compass**. {{hud-compass}}

items: A strip at the top left, under the status line, shows N, E, S and W around the way you face.
Your saved places show on the strip as small amber marks while they are within 90 degrees of your facing.
A cyan triangle points to the nearest known landmark: an expedition site or your locator pin. The line below names it, gives its distance and counts your pins.
Like the rest of the HUD, it hides in clean view ([[F1]]) and while a panel is open.

sections.title: Get back to a lost build

items: Stand at the build and open the Journal. Type a name in the **Name** box, then press **Pin this location**.
Before you travel far, select the place and press **Show on map** to check where it sits.
To return, click the place in the Journal to make it your destination. Then follow the beacon, the on-screen diamond or the amber mark on the HUD compass.

blocks.text: The maps show terrain, not your builds. A destination pin is the way back when a build is hard to recognise in the terrain.
