items: Select a block in the hotbar with keys 1 to 0, or pick it from the Build catalog in creative.
Aim at the face where you want the block. A see-through ghost of the block, in its own texture, shows the cell it will fill.
Right-click to place one block. The held item must be a block. With a bow, rifle or throwing rock in hand, right-click aims or throws instead.

blocks.text: A whole block is eight half-metre pieces. In survival, each whole block uses 8 pieces of that material from your pack, and the game says so if you are short. Creative placement is free. {{whole-block-placement}}

If any part of the target cell is occupied, the whole block is refused and a red outline shows instead of the ghost. You cannot place a block inside yourself. Plants and water in the target cell are overwritten, except bamboo. Furniture between you and the block stops the click too: the status line says "Furniture blocks that placement", or "Furniture blocks that mining target" when you mine, and nothing is spent. See {{guide:furniture-and-carpentry|Furniture and carpentry}}.

In creative, middle-click the block you aim at to pick it. If the block is already in a hotbar slot, that slot is selected. Otherwise the block is held without changing your other slots. Aiming at a door picks the closed door. Middle-click does nothing in survival. {{middle-click-pick}}

Your aim passes through water to the first block beyond it. Stand on the shore and aim at a lake or sea bed, then build up from it. You cannot click the water surface itself. Placed blocks replace water and plants in their cell. {{building-in-water}}
A block is not placed when:

items: For ordinary block placement, select a block. Furniture, doors and chests have their own placement steps below.
Your hands are empty, or a tool, bow, rifle or throwing rock is in hand. No ghost shows and nothing happens.
A solid block, an open door leaf or bamboo is in the target cell: "That space is already occupied".
Furniture stands between you and the block: "Furniture blocks that placement".
In survival, your pack does not have 8 pieces of the material for a whole block (1 for a half-metre piece): "Need 8 ... pieces to place a block".

In creative, the world already holds 200,000 changed half-metre pieces, the save limit: "Save edit budget reached". From 190,000 the status line warns you. Survival building is not stopped, but a world past 200,000 can no longer be saved. {{placement-restrictions}}

blocks.text: The Water block in the creative catalog is a flowing source. Right-click with Water selected to place one. It spreads up to 7 half-metre cells sideways into open air and pours down over edges. {{flowing-water}}

items: Placing a block into water replaces that water cell.
Fill the source cell, or cut the stream off with a block, and the water it fed drains away cell by cell. Water on the source side of a new block stays.
Digging next to the sea or a lake lets water flow into the new gap. Natural seas and lakes never drain.
Survival players cannot pick up or place water. There are no buckets.
The other five water types are blocks. They do not flow.

blocks.text: To get rid of unwanted flowing water, place a block in the cell where you put the Water source. On a multiplayer server the server runs the water.

Hold [[Shift]] to place or mine one half-metre piece instead of a whole cube. The ghost shrinks to that piece. In creative, press [[N]] to toggle detail size without holding Shift; press N again for whole blocks. The status line says **Detail building: 0.5 m** or **Whole blocks: 1 m**. This lets you keep flying level while building small details. {{half-metre-detail-building}}

rows: Place one half-metre piece. In survival it uses one piece.
Carve one half-metre piece from a block. Logs and cactus still fell the whole tree or stem.
Clean view. Hides the ghost, outlines and HUD while you play.

blocks.text: Holding Shift also sneaks on foot, dives in water and descends while flying.

Doors are built from boards. They come in three styles and two sizes. A small door is one metre wide and two metres tall, with one leaf. A wide door is two metres wide and three metres tall, with two one-metre leaves. {{doors}}
Choose a door to craft

Open [[E]] > Craft and select any door recipe in the Timber section. Three buttons appear above the preview: **Style**, **Wood** and **Size**. Click one, or move keyboard focus to it and press [[Enter]], to step to its next choice. The other two choices stay as they are. {{door-styles-and-moves}}

items: **Style:** Plain, Panelled or Windowed. Panelled doors have framed, recessed panels. Windowed doors have glass panes in the upper part.
**Wood:** Alder, Birch, Pine, Oak, Fruitwood, Acacia, Willow, Mangrove, Jungle, Cherry, Giant, Palm, Mesquite, Fig or Cypress. A door of a named wood needs boards of exactly that wood.
**Any boards** is the original Wooden door. It takes boards of any wood, mixed if you like, and comes in Plain only. The Style button is greyed out until you choose a wood.
**Size:** 1 x 2 m for one leaf, or 2 x 3 m for two leaves.

Changing a choice only selects a different recipe. Doors you carry or have hung, and crafts already queued, stay as they are. If a recipe filter would hide your choice, the filter turns off and the status line says "Showing all recipes".

blocks.text: Costs are the same for every wood:

items: **Plain or Panelled, 1 x 2 m:** one block of boards (8 half-metre pieces).
**Plain or Panelled, 2 x 3 m:** two blocks of boards (16 pieces).
**Windowed, 1 x 2 m:** 6 board pieces and 2 glass pieces.
**Windowed, 2 x 3 m:** 12 board pieces and 4 glass pieces.

blocks.text: Recipe names follow your choices, for example Oak door, Wide panelled oak door or Windowed birch door. The original two are Wooden door and Wide wooden door.
Hang, open and take down

items: Hold the door and right click solid ground to hang it. The spot needs free space and solid ground under it. A player or animal standing where the leaves would go also stops the hang.
Right click a hung door to open it, and right click again to close it. A door swings away from the player who opens it, from either side. It has its own opening and closing sound.

The leaves turn on their hinges over 0.35 seconds, easing in and settling gently. If the leaves are not drawn on screen yet, for example while the chunk is still being rebuilt, the swing waits up to one second; a wide door across a chunk edge then turns both halves together. Using a door again while it is moving turns it back from where it stands.
A door will not open if anything other than air, water or plants is in its swing path. It also will not open while you or an animal stands where the leaves sweep. Clear the space and try again.

An open leaf stands a metre out of the doorway. You and walking animals cannot walk through it, and you cannot place a block into the space it stands in. Undo and redo refuse a change to that space too.
You cannot close a door while you stand in its opening. Step out first. A door will not shut while an animal stands in its opening.

Mine any leaf to take the whole door down; in Survival, hold left click until it comes down. In Survival the door goes back into your pack if there is room; if the pack is full, it is left hanging. Mining a block next to an open leaf leaves the door standing.
In Creative, middle click a door to hold one of the same style, wood and size. This works on either leaf, and on an open door.

blocks.text: Move a door (Creative)

items: Close the door and wait for it to stop swinging. Put tools away and use ordinary block building, not a brush.
Aim at the door and press [[Shift]] + left click. A blue outline marks the original door, which stays where it is for now.
Aim at clear, solid ground. The ghost shows where the door will stand. Press [[R]] to give it a quarter turn.
Right click to move the door. The status line says "Moved door | Ctrl+Z undoes".
To cancel, left click or press [[B]]. The original door is left as it was.

blocks.text: [[Ctrl+Z]] puts a moved door back and [[Ctrl+Shift+Z]] moves it again. Finish or cancel a move before you undo.

The new spot must be empty air, with no water or plants, and every leaf needs solid ground under it. You must move or turn the door, and nobody may stand where it will go. If the status line says "Move only a complete closed door after it stops swinging", close the door, wait and try again. Undo and Redo are refused if the door or its space has changed since.

On a server, doors can be hung, opened and taken down once the server accepts the action. In Survival, hanging spends one matching door after the server confirms, and taking one down returns the matching door. In Creative on a server, door moves, Undo and Redo work too: each step waits for the server to confirm, and a move waits while another server action is unfinished. A door move from before you respawned cannot be undone. Blueprints skip door leaves, so a door is not copied.
A wooden chest is one metre cube of storage. It keeps items where you set it down, so you can leave things at a build site. {{wooden-chests}}

items: **Wooden chest:** one block of boards of any wood. Craft it in the Timber section.
Hold the chest and right click to set it down. It fills the metre cell under the ghost, with the latch toward you.
Right click a chest within 6 m to open its Chest tab. Your pack and the chest sit side by side. The lid makes an opening sound, and a closing sound when the Chest tab shuts or you walk out of reach.
Click an item to move one across. Shift+click moves as much of that item as fits.
A chest holds up to 250 kg and up to 64 kinds of item. A world holds at most 512 chests.
To take a chest up, mine it. In Survival it goes back into your pack with everything inside, but only if the pack has room for all of it. In Creative, empty it first; you get no chest item back.

blocks.text: Refinish a chest
You can give a placed chest new woods for its body, lid and fittings. Its contents stay inside. {{chest-refinishing}}

items: Equip the Furniture hammer, aim at a placed chest within 6 m, and press [[E]] or right click.
The Refinish chest panel opens in the Build tab, starting with oak. Use the **Body**, **Lid** and **Fittings** buttons to choose each wood. Any of the fifteen woods works.
Press **Apply changes**. **Cancel**, or closing the panel, keeps the original chest as it was.

blocks.text: In Survival, refinishing costs 4 boards of the body wood, 3 of the lid wood and 1 of the fittings wood: one block of boards when all three match. The old chest supplies the box. Creative is free.

[[Ctrl+Z]] turns it back into the original chest with the same contents and, in Survival, returns the boards. [[Ctrl+Shift+Z]] applies the finish again. Both need the same game mode, with the contents and woods as they were right after the change. In Survival, Undo needs room in your pack for the boards, and Redo needs the boards again.

A refinished chest is storage furniture. Right click opens it, and it holds up to 250 kg and 64 kinds of item. Empty it before taking it up. Taking up one refinished in Survival returns the chest and its boards. The **Chest** plan in the carpentry workbench (the Wooden chest plan) makes the same kind of chest from one you carry: in Survival it costs one Wooden chest plus the same boards, and Creative is free.

On a server, wait for the server to confirm each chest action. You can set chests down, open them, move items and refinish them in Survival or Creative. In Survival, hold left click to take a chest up with its contents, if your pack has room. In Creative, empty it first; taking it up gives no chest item. On a server, a refinish from before you respawned or reconnected cannot be undone. Blasts, tracks, brushes, copy and blueprints leave chest cells alone.

Chairs, tables, desks, sofas, kitchen units, bathroom fixtures, storage furniture, beds and lamps are built from reusable furniture plans. In Survival, carry a **Furniture hammer** from E > Craft > Tools & arms; in Creative, pick a plan in the Build catalogue. Survival pays for the chosen materials when you place a piece. Plans, materials, moving, table joins and lanterns on tables are explained in {{guide:furniture-and-carpentry|Furniture and carpentry}}.

In creative mode, press B to move to the next brush. The order is Block, Line, Wall, Floor, Replace, Copy, Blueprint, Bench, Railing and Roof. After Roof, B selects the Chair furniture plan, and B again goes back to Block. The **Tool** button in E > Build > + Tools also steps to the next brush. {{creative-brush-cycle}}

items: Block: Right-click to place one block.
Line: Right-click once to set the first corner, aim at the far end and right-click again. The line follows the longer direction. {{brush-line-wall-floor}}
Wall: Same two clicks. The wall stands upright along the longer horizontal direction.
Floor: Same two clicks. The floor stays level at the height of the first corner.

Replace: Aim at a block of the material to swap and right-click. Aim at the opposite corner and right-click again. Matching blocks in the box become the block in your hand. If the box holds none, the status line says "0 matching pieces". {{brush-replace}}

Copy: Right-click two opposite corner blocks to copy the box, at most 512 half-metre pieces (for example 4 by 4 by 4 m). Air, the Home crate, chests and doors are left out; water and plants are copied. A box that takes in furniture is refused. Each further right-click pastes a copy at the ghost. R turns the paste 90 degrees. B discards the copy. In the Structure workshop, only blocks you placed are copied. {{brush-copy-paste}}
Blueprint: Save a build, then place it again. See the Blueprints section. {{creative-blueprints}}

Bench, Railing, Roof: One right-click stamps a fixed half-metre shape at the ghost: a 2 m bench, a 3.5 m railing or a 3 by 3 m stepped roof. Press R first to turn it 90 degrees. {{brush-bench-railing-roof}}

blocks.text: Every brush except Block shows a ghost first, red if the build would be refused. One action changes at most 512 half-metre pieces (64 whole blocks). Blueprints have their own limits. If a cell holds a solid block, a chest, a door or the Home crate, nothing is built and the status line says "Selection blocked". Water and plants do not block a build. Replace is the exception: it swaps only the material you aim at. Hold Shift (or use N) on the first click for half-metre steps.
Pressing B clears a corner selection or a copied selection. Copies are lost when you change brush or leave the world.

A blueprint is a build you save and place again. In creative mode it is free to place. In survival, placing it uses pieces from your pack. On a server, Creative players can place blueprints too; in Survival on a server, placement is refused with "Survival blueprints aren't available on servers yet".
Save a blueprint (creative)

items: Press [[B]] until the brush says **Blueprint**. You can also pick it in **E > Build**.
Aim at a ground corner of the build and press [[Shift]] + right-click. The status says **First corner set**.

Aim at the opposite ground corner and press [[Shift]] + right-click again. The **Structures** panel opens with a picture of what was taken. Nothing is saved yet. Until then, each corner you marked shows a post, and the box that would be saved is outlined. To cancel, press [[Shift]] + right-click on the same corner again.

Type a name (up to 32 characters) and press **Save** or [[Enter]]. A name that is taken needs a second press to replace it. **Keep both** saves a copy called Name 2. **Discard**, or closing the panel, throws the capture away.
If you just placed a saved blueprint, its name is filled in and the panel says **Enter updates it**. Press **Enter**, then **Enter** again, to replace that file. Type another name to keep both.
Aim where you want it. The ghost shows the result, centred on the cell you aim at. Right-click to build it. The whole build is one undo step, so [[Ctrl]]+[[Z]] removes it.

blocks.text: Build a blueprint in survival

items: Press [[B]] to take the Blueprint tool out. Press [[B]] again to put it away. In survival it is the only build tool, so [[B]] is the only key you need.
Aim where you want the build. The ghost turns red when you lack pieces.
Check the list on screen. It shows each material as carried / needed.
Right-click to build. The build is paid for in one go, or refused whole.

blocks.text: Each half-metre piece you change costs one piece of the item that block drops when mined. A whole block is 8 pieces. Dirt-type turf costs dirt. Voxels that already hold the right block cost nothing. If you lack any material, nothing is built or spent, and the status names the missing items. The Shift + right-click save also works in survival, by the game source; it is not checked in play.

rows: Lift the ghost 1 m up or down, up to 64 m.
Delete the selected blueprint and its file.

blocks.text: The save leaves out water, cells you carved out of the terrain, the Home crate, chests and doors. The panel says how many cells were left out. A box that takes in furniture saves nothing: move or take up the furniture first. A blueprint can be up to 128 m along any side and 16,384 half-metre pieces, and you can keep up to 64. Placement builds over natural ground, plants and water. It is refused if it would build over blocks you placed yourself or the Home crate, or around you ("Step back: it would be built around you").

Saved blueprints are plain files with the `.blueprint` extension in a folder named `blueprints`, in the folder the game starts from. The game makes it when you save your first blueprint, and every world shares it.

On a server, a Creative blueprint appears at once and the server then confirms it; if the server refuses, the build is taken away again. Every piece must be within 64 m of you, each build waits a moment after the last ("Blueprints wait a moment between builds"), and very large blueprints are refused ("Too large to build on a server at once").
Structure workshop

Choose **Structure workshop** on the main menu to open the structure library. Pick a saved structure and choose **Open structure**, or choose **Create new**, type a name and choose **Create structure**. Your current world is saved before the editor opens.

The structure opens on flat ground in its own editor. It is always creative, at midday, with no animals, and it is not saved as a world. Build with the ordinary controls. Press [[F6]] to save the structure to your blueprints; a structure you opened is replaced by the new version. Press [[Esc]] to go back to the library. With unsaved changes you choose **Save and exit**, **Discard** or **Cancel**.

F6 saves only blocks. The save is refused, with the reason in the status line, while the editor holds furniture, water, a chest, a door or ground you dug away. The structure editor has not been checked in play yet. This page follows the game source and its tests.

In the library, **Rename** changes a name, **Duplicate** saves an independent copy, and **Delete structure** removes one after you hold it for 3 seconds. **Back** returns to the main menu, where **Continue** takes you back to your world.

Workshops made before the structure library are listed in **Worlds** with **(legacy workshop)**. Opening one keeps its original terrain, platform, player position and builds. Choose **Leave workshop** on the main menu to return to the world you came from.
Move a build from a legacy workshop

items: Open the legacy workshop from **Worlds**.
Save the build as a blueprint (see Save a blueprint, creative above).
Choose **Leave workshop** to return to your world, then choose **Structure workshop** on the main menu.
In the library, select the saved blueprint and choose **Open structure** to check it in the editor.
Keep the legacy workshop until you have checked the copy. It stays available for more edits.

blocks.text: Sharing or importing blueprints is not in this version. It is tracked in the {{structure-workshop-blueprints|feature ledger}}.
With the Blueprint tool out, press [[O]] to open the library. Each saved structure has its own picture. The picked one is shown large, with its size and piece count.

rows: Open the library, or close it again.
Pick the previous or next structure.
Close the library with the picked structure ready to aim.
Delete the picked structure. Press it twice to confirm.

blocks.text: Click the name to rename a structure; **Rename** or [[Enter]] saves the new name. Rename writes the new file before the old one is removed, so a failed rename keeps the original. The library holds up to 64 structures. Click the search field above the list and type part of a name to narrow it. Enter ends the search and keeps the matches, and Up and Down pick among them.
Source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46. Not yet play-tested for this guide.

rows: The same actions, in the E > Build tab (Creative).

blocks.text: In Creative, undo covers brush actions, blueprints, single blocks placed and blocks or trees you mined. Door moves, chest refinishing and furniture steps go into the same history, so [[Ctrl+Z]] always takes back your newest step first. The status line says what it undid, for example "Undid building" or "Undid door move". The history holds your last 32 steps at most. On a server, undoing a door move, chest refinishing or furniture step waits for the server to confirm. {{build-undo-redo}}

Undo is refused with "Undo blocked" if the cells changed since or if it would put a block inside you. At the save's edit limit it says "Save edit budget reached". It also stops, and says why, where a chest, door, furniture or the Home crate is in the way. Survival block edits and explosions are not recorded, but in Survival [[Ctrl+Z]] still undoes furniture steps and chest refinishing; see {{guide:furniture-and-carpentry|Furniture and carpentry}}. History is cleared when you leave the world.

In creative, E > Build has the searchable catalog. Choose **+ Tools** to open the brush controls, Undo and Redo, four preset palettes and Save palette. Survival gains a restricted carpentry Build tab while a Furniture hammer is in your pack. {{creative-catalog}} {{build-workspace-palettes}}

items: Click an ordinary catalog item to take one. Shift-click to take as many as fit in your pack. Furniture plans select a reusable construction choice instead of adding a carried item.
Right-click an item to remove one you carry. Shift-right-click removes all of them.
Middle-click an item to star it. Starred items are listed under **STARRED**.
Click the search box, or press [[Ctrl+F]], and type part of a name. Enter ends typing; right-click the box to clear it.
Hover an item and press 1 to 0, or drag it onto a slot, to bind it to the hotbar.
In creative, open **+ Tools**, then click Timber, Masonry, Coastal or Garden to fill the ten quick slots with that set. Slot 1 is selected.
Click Save palette to store your current ten slots.
Shift-click Save palette to load them back.

blocks.text: A preset replaces all ten quick slots. Click Save palette first if you want to keep them.

guides.title: Sailing a boat
guides.headline:
Launch it, steer it,
read the wind.
guides.summary: Launch and pack up the Small sailing boat, take the helm, set the sails, tack upwind, read the sailing panel and save your boats.
guides.lead: The Small sailing boat floats on any water in the game. You launch it from the hotbar, steer it from the helm and set the sails to catch the wind. Boats are not available on multiplayer servers yet.
