blocks.text: Craft the Small sailing boat from the Timber recipes. Crafting it selects it, ready to launch. In Creative, take it from the catalog. The boat floats on any water: sea, lakes and all six water types, at their real surface height. {{sailing-launch-and-pack}}

items: Select the Small sailing boat in your hotbar or inventory.
Look at open water within 6 m and right-click. The boat appears on the water, facing the way you look.
In Survival, the launch uses one boat item. In Creative, no item is used.

blocks.text: The launch needs water under the whole hull, no blocks in the way of the hull or mast, and space clear of other boats. If it fails, the game says "Boat needs clear water and room for its hull and mast (8 boats maximum)" and nothing is used. You can have up to 8 boats in the world at once.
Packing a boat puts it back into your pack, so you can carry it to another lake or sea. {{sailing-launch-and-pack}}

items: Walk up to a boat that has nobody at the helm and look at it from within 6 m.
Hold [[Shift]] and right-click. You can hold any item.
The game says Sailing boat packed, and a Small sailing boat item goes into your pack, in Survival and in Creative.
You need 18 capacity of free pack room. Otherwise the game says "Free 18 capacity to pack the boat".
A boat with 0 HP (wrecked) cannot be boarded or packed. Wrecks are not saved, and the game clears them the next time you launch a boat.

blocks.text: Boats are not available on multiplayer servers yet. Launching or packing says "Boats aren't available on servers yet", and [[V]] says "Vehicles aren't available on servers yet".

You can walk and jump on the wooden deck like normal ground. The helm is where you steer and set the sails. Within 9 m of a boat, the hint by the crosshair reads PRESS V TO ENTER SMALL SAILING BOAT. {{sailing-helm-controls}}

rows: Take the helm, or step back to the cockpit. You must be within 9 m of the hull or on its deck.
Raise the sail setting. The sails follow over about 2 seconds.
Steer left or right. The rudder eases in and recentres.
Switch between first-person and chase view.
Look around freely. The view swings back when you let go.

items: There is no reverse. Lower the sails to slow down, and steer to turn.
The boat can turn slowly while it is stopped. It turns faster the faster it sails.

The boat stops dead if its hull would run aground or hit another boat. It can only turn where the new heading still has water under the whole hull. If the boat is stuck on the shore, pack it up and launch it again.
Stepping off the helm stops the boat at once, and the sails lower by themselves. A boat with nobody at the helm does not drift.
At the helm, [[E]] does not open your pack and map travel is refused. Press [[V]] to step off first.

blocks.text: Each world has one wind direction, and it never changes. The wind strength depends on the weather: about 2.8 m/s in clear weather and up to 8.5 m/s in a thunderstorm. Seasons do not change the wind. {{sailing-wind-and-tacking}}

items: Running with the wind (sailing straight downwind) is fastest. The boat reaches the wind speed, up to its top speed of 6 m/s.
Sailing across the wind gives about two-thirds of the wind speed.
Within 45 degrees of sailing straight into the wind, the sails give no push. To go upwind, zig-zag: sail one side of the wind, then turn across it to the other side. This is called tacking.
Lower sails give less speed. Half sail gives half the speed.

blocks.text: Read the flags and the panel

items: The red pennant at the top of the mast points downwind, the way the air travels.
At the helm, a panel titled SAILBOAT sits at the top left, under the status line. Its flag box shows the same wind with the bow of your boat at the top.
WIND n M/S TO n gives the wind speed and the compass bearing the air blows towards: 0 is north, 90 east, 180 south and 270 west.
The panel says TACK: TURN ACROSS WIND when your bow is in the no-push zone, and BOW UP FLAG otherwise.
The line above shows the boat's HP, its speed in knots (KN), the sail setting (TRIM) and your compass heading (HDG).

blocks.text: Up to 8 launched boats are saved with the world, with their position, heading and health. Your boats are still there when you load the world. {{sailing-saving}}
If you save while at the helm, you reload standing in the stopped boat's cockpit, not at the helm. Press V to take the helm again.

guides.title: Settings and performance
guides.headline:
Settings,
and how to make the game run smoothly.
guides.summary: Find graphics, audio, controls and interface preferences, change keys and reduce rendering work.
guides.lead: In a world, press Esc and choose Settings; on the start menu, choose Settings directly. Most preferences follow you between worlds.

verification.method: Every Settings group, page, option name, range, default and help text, the graphics presets, search and reset, key capture, the F3/F7/F8/F9 overlays, audio mixing, nature-ambience rules and the shared preference file were re-checked against Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480 source on 2026-11-08. Normal-window GPU timing remains separate from offscreen developer profiling.
verification.limits: Source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested. No FPS or GPU-memory benchmark, desktop idle test or new screenshot was made. Old hardware figures are not presented as current results.

items: In a world, press Esc and choose Settings. On the start menu, choose Settings directly. Ctrl+F on the pause menu opens Settings with search ready.
Choose Graphics, Audio, Controls, Gameplay, Interface or Advanced, then a subpage.

Click Find settings or press Ctrl+F, then type. A setting matches when every word appears in its group, page, name or help. Enter or Tab leaves the field; Up/Down then steps through matches on every page. Ctrl+Backspace clears the search.

rows: Previous / next subpage; on Key bindings, previous / next page of actions.
Select a row or search result.
Step the selected value back / forward.
Click a chip or < >, drag a slider
Restore this page’s defaults, outside text entry. On Key bindings, Backspace or Reset keys restores every key.

blocks.text: Changes apply immediately. Hover a label for help. Back or Esc returns to the pause menu or start menu; Resume returns to play. Local play pauses; connected servers continue. {{settings-menu}}

items: **Graphics > Display** holds Graphics preset, Field of view, Horizon distance, Atmospheric fog, Frame limit, Shader and Chunk fade-in.

**Graphics preset** sets five of them at once. Low: Shader None, 32 chunks, Dense fog, no fade-in, 60 FPS. Balanced (the defaults): Fast, 64 chunks, Balanced fog, fade-in, 60 FPS. High: Fast, 128 chunks, Balanced fog, fade-in, 120 FPS. Cinematic: Cinematic, 192 chunks, Light fog, fade-in, 60 FPS. Editing one of those five shows Custom; Field of view is not part of a preset.

**Shader** offers None, Fast (default) or Cinematic. None is plain voxel lighting; Fast adds sun shadows, sun rays and haze; Cinematic refines shadows and rays and adds reflective water, at extra frame time. {{shader-tiers}}

**Horizon distance** offers 8, 16, 32, 48, 64 (default), 96, 128, 192, 256, 512 and 1024 chunks. One chunk is 16 m; the largest radius is about 16 km. It sets only the low-detail distant view; full-detail terrain near you stays at nine chunks. {{horizon-distance}}
**Frame limit** is 60 (default), 120, 240 or Unlimited. A cap is not a guaranteed frame rate. There is no separate vsync setting; Frame limit paces the frames. {{frame-limit}}

**Atmospheric fog** is Light, Balanced (default) or Dense; haze strength follows Horizon distance. **Field of view** is 60–96° in 2° steps (default 72°). **Chunk fade-in** (on by default) fades newly loaded terrain in over 0.6 seconds. {{atmospheric-fog}} {{field-of-view}} {{chunk-fade-in}}
**Controls > Mouse** has separate Horizontal and Vertical sensitivity (50–200% in 10% steps, default 100%) and Invert mouse Y.

**Controls > Key bindings** changes gameplay keys. Select an action and press Enter (or click it), then press the new key. Esc cancels and Delete leaves the action unbound. Esc, F6, F11 and Print Screen cannot be assigned. A key used by two actions shows “Conflict: …”. Defaults are in {{guide:controls-reference|Controls reference}}.
**Gameplay > Movement** has Camera bob, Speed FOV, Damage bob (Off, Reduced or Full) and Hold/Toggle for Sprint, Sneak and Crawl. Sprint and Sneak default to Hold; Crawl defaults to Toggle.

**Interface > Layout** has GUI size (Auto, Small, Normal or Large), UI scale (75–200% in 5% steps), HUD text only, Target info (F2), HUD compass and Compact map heading. Scale is capped so the menu fits. {{gui-size}}
**Interface > Crosshair** sets style (Cross, Dot or Brackets), size (50–200%), colour (Adaptive, White, Lime or Cyan) and opacity (25–100%). Every style keeps accuracy feedback.

**Interface > Accessibility** has Color vision palettes for information overlays, High contrast, Reduce motion, Low survival warning and Warning pulse. The warning appears when health, food, water or stamina falls to 10, 20, 30 or 40% (default 20%). Reduce motion turns off camera bob, FOV kick, blast shake, fades and pulses; static warnings remain.

**Audio > Volume** has Master, Music, Effects, Ambience and UI volume, each 0–100% (default 100%). Arrow keys move them 5% at a time. Master scales every category; zero on one category mutes only that category. {{master-volume}}

**Audio > Music** turns music on or off, sets Music speed from 0.5× to 2.0× in 0.1× steps (tempo and pitch; effects keep their speed) and picks the Previous or Next song. Below it you see the current title, “No music installed”, or a sound problem: “Sound unavailable: install alsa-utils” on Linux, or “install ffplay (FFmpeg)” on Windows and macOS. {{music-player}}

blocks.text: Set Ambience volume to zero to silence nature sounds while keeping effects and music. Nature sounds continue behind in-world menus but stop underwater and on the start menu. {{nature-ambience}}

**Advanced > Diagnostics** has LOD view, Voxel view, Distant terrain, Performance, Chunk borders and FPS and coordinates; Mesh view is shown as unavailable. The FPS box is on by default and shows measured FPS with the limit (or UNCAPPED), your X, Y and Z position and the biome. It hides while a menu is open. {{fps-coordinates-readout}}

rows: Show or hide the performance overlay: CPU work over the last half second, frame time against the frame budget, the worst recent frame and a spike count. The budget follows Frame limit (Unlimited uses 60 FPS); a spike is a frame over twice the budget and at least 25 ms.
Show or hide 16 m chunk borders. Your current chunk is gold; neighbours are cyan.
Cycle the LOD view: Off, Tint and Colors. With the standard palette, cyan is full detail; green, blue, yellow, orange, purple and red mark the 0.5 to 16 m distant stages.
Turn all three overlays off if any is on; otherwise turn all on, with LOD view in Tint.

blocks.text: The keys above are defaults and can be reassigned. Performance, Chunk borders and LOD view are not saved: after a restart they are off, and the FPS box is on again. {{diagnostic-overlays}} {{performance-overlay}}

items: **Voxel view**: Off (default), Edges, which tints every block border, or X-ray, which draws only the outlines. {{voxel-view}}

**Distant terrain**: on by default. It draws the low-detail horizon beyond the nearby chunks. Turning it off saves work on slow machines. The view then ends at the nearby loaded terrain, where new chunks appear as you move. {{distant-terrain-toggle}}
Try Graphics > Display > Graphics preset > Low: plain shading, 32-chunk horizon, dense fog, no terrain fade and a 60 FPS limit.
If needed, lower Horizon distance to 16 or 8 chunks, or turn Advanced > Diagnostics > Distant terrain off. The distant view becomes shorter.
Use the default F3 key to compare frame time with the frame budget. Compare the same place and settings before drawing conclusions.

blocks.text: The normal window does not provide live GPU pass timings. This guide has no current hardware benchmark or promised frame-rate gain. {{performance-overlay}}

Graphics, audio, interface preferences and key bindings follow the player between worlds. They save automatically about half a second after a change and when you quit; on Linux the file is ~/.config/voxelgame/settings. If it cannot be read, the game leaves it untouched, stops saving preferences and shows “Settings not saved …”; fix the file and restart. Time, weather and season belong to each world, under Gameplay > World; they are read-only in survival. For profile locations and recovery, see {{guide:install-and-worlds|Install, update and find your worlds}}. {{per-world-settings}}
The 1024-chunk horizon is available as an optional distant view. No current hardware performance result is supplied here. {{horizon-1024}}
Live GPU pass timings in ordinary play remain planned. The normal window’s GPU box reports unavailable. {{gpu-timing-live}}

The native app requests that the desktop stay awake while its window is focused and visible, including menus. Desktop support varies; it releases the request on focus loss or hiding. {{display-awake}}

guides.title: Explosives: TNT and dynamite
guides.headline:
Blow up blocks
with TNT and dynamite.
guides.summary: Place and light TNT with G, read the blast and damage reach, throw dynamite, and craft both in Survival.
guides.lead: TNT and dynamite break blocks in a wide circle. Blasted blocks are destroyed, not collected. Creative players can use them freely. In Survival you craft both from sand, Charcoal, boards and Paper screens.

verification.method: On 8 November 2026 every section was re-checked against the game source at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480: game.rs (G, group lighting, detonation, damage and knockback), explosives.rs (blast reach, the 512-piece limit, lit-charge movement, cover), explosion_terrain.rs (crater and chain lighting), world/block.rs (blast resistance), game/explosion_loot.rs (animals), game/ranged_input.rs and projectile.rs (dynamite), inventory.rs (recipes), session/tnt.rs, session/tnt/dynamite.rs, game/net_client/tnt.rs, game/net_client/dynamite_throws.rs and docs/MULTIPLAYER.md (servers). Blast and damage distances are calculated from code constants, not measured in play.
verification.limits: Source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested. No server session was run. No explosion screenshots exist yet, so the blast sizes are not checked against a headless capture.

items: Select TNT in your hotbar.
Right click a surface to place a whole block. Hold Shift and right click to place one half-metre charge.
Aim at the TNT, within 6 m, and press [[G]].
Step back. The fuse lasts 2.6 seconds.

rows: Light the aimed TNT and every TNT piece touching it, even diagonally.
Mine TNT back without lighting it.

blocks.text: Lit TNT pops loose and can fall, roll or float before it blows. Touching pieces go off together as one blast. One press lights at most 64 whole blocks (512 pieces). {{tnt-place-and-ignite}}

On a multiplayer server, [[G]] asks the server to light the TNT. The status line says "Requesting TNT ignition | move away"; wait for the reply before your next action. The server checks that you can reach the TNT, and that no piece of the group is on land you may not build on or holds up furniture. It then says, for example, "8-charge TNT cluster ignited by server | move away". A refusal starts with "TNT ignition refused:" and gives the reason. If the server restarts while a fuse burns, that TNT is lost.

items: One half-metre charge or one dynamite stick: about 1.5 m.
One whole TNT block: about 4.25 m.
A touching group of TNT: up to about 10.5 m, which needs about 62 touching TNT blocks.

blocks.text: A whole TNT block cannot break obsidian. Solid stone only gives way close to the charge. Blocks between the charge and a target absorb part of the blast, and water absorbs a lot of it. Water is never destroyed, and chests survive every blast. Other TNT inside the blast is lit on a short fuse of under a second and thrown outward. {{explosion-effects}}

In a single-player world a blast breaks your own builds too. On a multiplayer server it leaves doors, chests and the blocks that hold up furniture alone, breaks nothing on land the person who lit it may not build on, and does not hurt players or animals standing there.
Explosions cannot be undone. Blasted blocks are gone. The status line counts cleared half-metre voxels.

In Survival, players near a blast lose health and are knocked back. Creative players take no damage and are not pushed. Creatures are hurt in both modes. In Survival, an animal killed by a blast drops its items on the ground; in Creative it is removed.

Damage reaches about one and a half times as far as the blast breaks blocks: about 2.3 m for a half-metre charge or dynamite stick, about 6.6 m for one TNT block and about 16 m for the largest group. It is strongest close to the charge, and walls between you and the charge reduce it.
Stand well back before you light a group. Damage reaches about 16 m from the largest group.

items: Select Dynamite in your hotbar.
Hold right click to wind up. A longer wind-up throws farther; full power takes 0.7 seconds.
Release to throw. The fuse starts on release.
Take cover. The stick goes off 2.3 seconds after you throw it, wherever it is then.

rows: Wind up and throw a dynamite stick.

items: The stick sticks to the first surface it hits, including walls, ceilings and furniture. If that surface is dug or blown away, the stick falls again.
A very short wind-up does not throw. The status line says "Too hasty — wind up before releasing".
You cannot place blocks while you hold dynamite.
Opening a menu cancels a wind-up.
Creative throws are unlimited. Survival uses one stick per throw. A throw that cannot fly keeps the stick.

On a multiplayer server, releasing asks the server to throw. The status line says "Requesting dynamite throw", then "Dynamite thrown by server". Wait for the reply before you throw again. A refused throw keeps the stick, for example "Wait for the server to finish the current action | dynamite kept". In Survival the server spends one stick when it accepts the throw; Creative throws stay free.

blocks.text: {{dynamite-throwing}}

sections.title: Crafting TNT and dynamite in Survival

blocks.text: One TNT recipe makes 8 pieces, one whole block. Two dynamite sticks need 4 TNT pieces and 2 Paper screens. Neither recipe needs Glow crystal. {{lumen-crystal-supply}}

sections.title: What a quit or reload does

items: Lit TNT and burning dynamite are not saved. Quitting during a fuse loses that TNT.
On a multiplayer server, lit TNT and burning dynamite are lost if the server restarts. Blasted ground, injuries and loot are kept.
Explosions are not recorded in build history.

guides.title: Day, night and weather
guides.headline:
Day, night and weather
what changes and when.
guides.summary: A day lasts 20 minutes. Weather follows a 30-minute pattern in every world, rain stops at roofs, and creative players can hold the time and weather.
guides.lead: A full day and night lasts 20 real minutes. Weather in a world follows the same 30-minute pattern, so you can plan around rain and storms. Nothing skips the night: the sun keeps moving, and you cannot sleep through it.

verification.method: Re-checked against the game source at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026: day length, start time and sun path (environment.rs, game.rs, frame.rs), the night sky (shader.wgsl), farm animals resting at night (entities), beds and Home rest leaving the clock alone (furniture/resting.rs, home.rs), the weather order, step length and blending, the rain, cloud, fog and wind of each weather, lightning and thunder timing (environment.rs), rain stopping at blocks and at the cloud ceiling (precipitation.rs), roof rain and wildlife sounds (ambience.rs), sailing wind (sailing.rs), the clock pausing in menus (game.rs), the shared server clock (session.rs, server host, net bridge) and the Gameplay > World rows (settings.rs, ui.rs, music_settings.rs, settings_search.rs). The cloud heights still match the native before/after captures and automated altitude tests recorded at Voxelgame 61a4257 on 15 October 2026; those captures were not repeated.
verification.limits: Source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested. No new captures were taken. No public weather or night photographs have been added.

blocks.text: One day and night lasts 20 real minutes. The sun is up for about 10 minutes and down for about 10. New worlds start about a minute after sunrise. {{day-night-cycle}}

items: Night is darker and the moon is out. On clear nights you also see stars and the Milky Way; cloud hides them. Nothing dangerous happens at night because of the time of day.
Cows, sheep, pigs and chickens stop wandering and rest on dry ground from about a minute after sunset until about a minute before sunrise. An animal you hit still runs.

You cannot sleep or skip the night. Lying in a bed does not pass time ({{guide:storage-beds-and-lamps|Storage, beds and lamps}}), and **Rest / set respawn** at your Home crate only sets your respawn point and refills stamina.

Birds sing near trees from sunrise until about midday. Night wildlife sounds take over after dark. Both are quieter in rain and silent under a roof, high above the ground, on coasts and in deserts, snowy or volcanic land.
In a single-player world, time stops while the pause menu, Settings or the fullscreen map is open. On a server the clock keeps running.

blocks.text: Day and night do not cause ambient-temperature survival penalties. {{temperature-shelter}}

items: The weather cycle takes 30 minutes. Each step lasts 3 minutes.
The order is clear, cloudy, rain, cloudy, partly cloudy, foggy, cloudy, rainstorm, thunderstorm, cloudy. Then it starts again.
Rain, cloud, mist and wind blend over about 15 seconds when the step changes, so there is no sudden switch.

blocks.text: Each world starts at a different point in the cycle. The whole world shares one weather pattern, so rain falls over deserts too. There is no snowfall. To see the current step, press [[Esc]], choose **Settings** and open **Gameplay > World**: the Weather row reads, for example, **Auto / rain**. {{automatic-weather}}

items: **Clear**: a cloudless sky. **Partly cloudy**: scattered clouds. **Cloudy**: grey overcast. None of them rain.
**Rain**: steady rain and a light breeze.
**Rainstorm**: heavy rain and strong wind, with no lightning.
**Thunderstorm**: the heaviest rain, the strongest wind, and lightning with thunder.
**Foggy**: thick mist that cuts visibility, with no rain.
Rain stops at the first solid or liquid block, so a roof you build keeps the rain off you.
Under a roof, rain is heard as a softer patter on the roof.
Overcast and rain darken the sky, and rain thickens the haze.
In a thunderstorm, lightning lights up the sky and land about every 18 seconds, and thunder follows one to three seconds later. Lightning does not damage you or set anything on fire.
Cloud banks begin at 1,200, 1,800 and 2,500 metres above world zero.
Rain and its sound fade as you climb through the lowest cloud bank and stop by 1,600 metres. Flying above the clouds does not stop rain in the world below.
Weather never hurts you. Rain, storms and fog have no health, food, water or temperature penalty.
The music leans towards songs that suit the time of day, rain, storms and fog.

blocks.text: Wind strength changes with the weather, from about 2.8 m/s in clear weather to 8.5 m/s in a thunderstorm, so sailing is affected too. {{sailing-wind-and-tacking}}

sections.title: Hold the time or weather in creative

items: Press [[Esc]], choose **Settings**, then open **Gameplay > World**.
On the **Time of day** row, click **<** or **>** to step through Cycle, Dawn, Day, Dusk and Night. Cycle goes back to the normal day.
On the **Weather** row, step through Auto, Clear, Partly cloudy, Cloudy, Rain, Rainstorm, Thunderstorm and Foggy. Auto goes back to the normal pattern.

rows: Hold the sun at sunrise, midday or sunset, or hold the moon at midnight.
Dry skies with no cloud, scattered cloud or overcast.
Steady rain, or heavy rain without lightning.
Heavy rain with lightning and thunder.

blocks.text: You can also pick a row with the Up / Down arrow keys and change it with Left / Right or [[Enter]]; right-click a row to step it back. Both lists wrap round. **Reset page** sets Time of day back to Cycle and Weather and Season back to Auto.

A held time or weather is saved with the world and stays in force if you switch to survival with [[F4]]. In survival the rows only show the current state; trying to change one says **Time, weather, and season controls are read-only in survival**. {{creative-world-controls}}
On a server, everyone shares the server's time, weather and season. Changes in this tab do not reach the server and are replaced within a few seconds.

sections.title: Planned, not in the game yet

blocks.text: Planned: darker nights, and regional weather where different parts of a world get different weather. Until these ship, the day length and weather pattern above are the same everywhere.

guides.title: Saves and world files
guides.headline:
Saves and world files
what is kept, and the limits.
guides.summary: Save, back up and recover a world. Find what persists and how the 200,000-block and 8 MiB limits apply.
guides.lead: Your world file keeps your character, carried items and changes to the world. Untouched terrain is rebuilt from the saved seed and generation. Display, audio and input preferences are shared across worlds.

verification.method: What a save keeps comes from the save writer's section list (crates/voxelgame-core/src/save/write.rs) and the session-only settings in the ledger. Limits and messages were checked against Voxelgame 51169272: 8 MiB and 200,000-edit constants and the 190,000 warning threshold (save.rs, game.rs), the 'saves' refusals and the version checks (save.rs, load.rs). Opening rules come from src/app.rs and src/single_instance.rs. Targeted compatibility clarification at 35cfc2f8: the serialized temperature field remains inert in survival.rs; other save evidence retains its original audit. Targeted 5 November source follow-up at aa136e0103ce5599c6d8a9f70c669dbc758b7357: current save sections, shared preferences, generation 12, Worlds backup/recovery and stopped-host retry/choice paths. Existing unrelated opening-screen evidence keeps its earlier check. The game’s dated WORLD_BACKUP_20261016 verification records offscreen backup recovery; it was not rerun for this guide. Targeted 8 November 2026 source follow-up at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c: F6 confirms only after a local write (src/app.rs), the 8 MiB refusal in the save encoder and writer (save.rs), size refusals on servers (session/crafting.rs, creatures.rs, items.rs, water.rs and home/*.rs), dedicated-server save waits (voxelgame-server host/furniture/durability/stock.rs), the seat and bed exit check before saving (save/write.rs, game/furniture/resting.rs, seating.rs) and saved lamp and stove state (furniture/lamp_state.rs, furniture/cooking.rs). The stopped-host recovery steps were re-checked on 8 November 2026 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480: voxelgame-render startup_ui/stopped_owner_choice.rs:16-61; voxelgame-core game/stopped_owner_choice.rs:132-230; src/net_client/ready_recovery/canonical_choice.rs:50-164; src/app.rs:1097-1108.
verification.limits: Source-checked in this follow-up; no new game process, native save/fault injection, LAN play or screenshot capture. Existing loading-screen prose retains its earlier audit. No game run has checked these backup and stopped-host steps. A session that has not been saved is not guaranteed to survive a restart. The 8 November follow-up was source-checked at Voxelgame dfeb362d on 8 November 2026; not play-tested, with no game process, server or save-fault run. The stopped-host recovery steps were source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested.

blocks.text: Saving writes the whole world file. It keeps:

items: Your position, view direction and game mode (creative or survival).
In survival: health, hunger, thirst and stamina. A legacy temperature value is retained for compatibility and has no gameplay effect.
Your inventory, hotbar bindings and selected slot, and the tool you hold.
Every block you changed, including water and door state.
Time of day, weather and season controls.
Your home crate and rest point, chest contents and one saved build palette.
Placed furniture with its stored items, whether each lamp is switched on, and a stove's contents and unfinished batch.
Journal places, expedition finds, milestones and the map destination.
Up to 8 sailing boats.
Player-hatched animals and dropped item stacks. {{save-contents}}

blocks.text: Procedural wildlife, flying projectiles and primed TNT are not saved. Temporary diagnostic overlays also reset. Display, audio and input preferences are shared separately; a world file still contains older settings fields for compatibility.

items: [[F6]] saves now. “World saved safely” appears only after the world file is written, including the world you host. In a world you joined, or a session started with --no-save, F6 writes nothing and says “This session does not save the world locally”.
Autosave checks about every 30 seconds and saves when world state has changed.
Choosing Main menu, Save & quit or Quit, pressing [[Ctrl]]+[[Q]], closing the window, or loading or creating another world saves first.
Main menu keeps a hosted world running. Use **Stop hosting** on the Multiplayer page to end hosting.

blocks.text: A failed save shows “Save refused:” with the reason and keeps a visible warning until a save succeeds. If saving fails while you are quitting, the game stays open so you can fix the problem and retry. {{saving}}

If you save while sitting or lying in a bed, the world reopens with you standing beside it. Saving needs a clear spot to stand there; otherwise it is refused with 'Bed exit blocked; cannot save an embedded player' or 'Seat exit blocked; cannot save an embedded player'. Make room and save again.
In a world you joined, the server keeps the world. A dedicated server confirms most actions only after it has saved them; see {{guide:not-in-the-game-yet|Multiplayer and feature limits}}.
If a stopped host cannot recover your pack

items: Keep the session open. If the save before stopping failed, the world is still hosted; fix the reported problem and try **Stop hosting** again.
If hosting has stopped and pack recovery is blocked, press [[F6]] to retry. **Continue** returns to the repair session so you can adjust conflicting Creative catalogue choices.

Press [[Shift]]+[[F6]] to open the recovery choice. **Keep current choices** (or [[Esc]]) changes nothing. To accept the host's final state, hold **Hold: use final pack** for 3 seconds with the mouse, [[Enter]] or [[Space]]: your pack and mode become the host's final ones, and conflicting Creative catalogue choices are set aside; your hotbar, tools and map pins stay as they are. If the final world or pack is unavailable, the choice is **Use last saved world** instead, also held for 3 seconds: the last saved world and its matching pack come back together, and later hosted changes are set aside.

Before switching, the game saves a separate recovery copy, with a RECOVERY.txt, in a **pack-recovery-copies** folder next to the world's save file, and names it on screen; keep it. If that copy cannot be written, your current choices stay as they are and the session stays open; follow the reported error before choosing again with [[Shift]]+[[F6]].

blocks.text: An unresolved pack blocks ordinary saving, world replacement and quitting. Recovery files next to the save belong to the unfinished recovery; do not delete them to get past the choice. The dialog explains which later state will be set aside. {{mp-menu-lan-hosting}}

items: Each world file is capped at 8 MiB. A save that would be bigger is refused with “Save refused: refusing to exceed the 8 MiB debug-save safety budget”, and the existing file stays as it was.
A world holds up to 200,000 changed blocks. Beyond that, new building is refused with 'Save edit budget reached'. Spreading water never pushes a save past the limit.
From 190,000 changed blocks, the status line warns 'saving stops at 200000' about every 20 seconds.
A home crate, blueprint or structure that would go past the limit is not placed.

On a hosted or dedicated server, the size cap also limits other actions, such as crafting, hitting animals, moving or dropping items and filling flasks. If the world file would go over, the server refuses with a message ending 'would exceed the save budget or saved state is invalid', for example 'Crafting would exceed the save budget or saved state is invalid'. An exact fit is allowed, and actions that make the save smaller still work.

blocks.text: Make and reopen a backup

items: Open **Worlds**, select a saved world and choose **Create backup** or press [[Ctrl]]+[[B]]. Stop hosting first if this is the hosted world.
Wait for **Backup ready** and keep the location shown. A completed backup ends in backups/backup-<time>-<process>-<sequence>/snapshot/. The active local world is saved before copying.
To reopen a backup, close the game and copy the whole completed **snapshot** folder into a new folder such as worlds/recovered-house/. Keep the original world and the backup.
Start the game and open the new copy from **Worlds**. A .pending folder is an unfinished attempt, not a completed backup.

blocks.text: Backups contain the save and its available name, preview and session-history files. They are stored beside worlds, so deleting the source world does not delete the backup. Finish any outstanding save recovery before making an ordinary backup or duplicate. {{world-backups}} {{save-limits}}

items: A world keeps the terrain generation it was created with. Create world defaults to generation 12 and also offers older generations; loading or updating a world preserves its saved choice. {{world-generation-version}}
A world saved before the half-metre block grid is refused with 'world predates the half-metre voxel grid; a new world is required'. Create a new world instead.
A world saved by a newer version of the game is refused by an older one with 'world was saved by a newer version of voxelgame'. Update the game to open it.
A file that is not a Voxelgame save is refused with 'not a voxelgame save'.

blocks.text: If a world will not open, read {{unreadable-save}}. {{save-compatibility}}

items: Only one copy of the game runs per user. Opening it again brings the open window to the front and shows 'Voxelgame was already open; click the world to recapture the mouse'. {{single-instance}}

When the game first opens, a tumbling wireframe cube settles into the Voxelgame logo above the current loading stage and an activity bar. Later world loads show only the stage and the bar. There is no percentage. {{loading-screen}}

guides.title: Animal spawning, calls and spawn eggs
guides.headline:
Animal spawning, calls and spawn eggs
where animals appear, and how to place them.
guides.summary: Wild animals appear around you as you explore, depending on the biome. Up to 36 can be around you at once. Creative mode has a spawn egg for each of the 94 species.
guides.lead: Wild animals appear on their own as you walk, sail and fly around the world. Which ones you see depends on the biome and nearby water. This page covers where animals appear, how many there can be, which species call, and how to use creative spawn eggs.

verification.method: Re-checked on 8 November 2026 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480. Spawning: crates/voxelgame-core/src/entities/mod.rs (36-animal cap at line 100; per-species caps at 677-710; the 25 squares of 32 m, the one-in-five empty squares, the 96 m height check, the water-depth rule and natural ground at 1696-1909; square memory at 1924-1955; 180 m removal at 1412-1420), entities/biome_species.rs:10-327 (biome species groups, swans, empty volcanic biomes), entities/ambient_spawn.rs:7-29 (natural ground) and session.rs:735-747 (one shared population on a server). Swimming: entities/aquatic_cruise.rs:164-278 and 324-367, and entities/mod.rs:1157-1167 (fish that keep their distance). Calls: entities/mod.rs:456-521 (the 57 calling species, re-checked at 21d656c2d5c32e82fd6287804078f391ef930657) and 1035-1076, game/audio.rs:157-191 and src/audio/effects.rs (hurt yelps and death sighs, at 21d656c2d5c32e82fd6287804078f391ef930657), events.rs:74-86 and 163-168, ambience.rs:190-209, entities/idle_behaviour.rs:15-19 and src/audio.rs:889-917. Species: Species::ALL (94 entries) and name() in entities/mod.rs:359-584. Eggs: ui.rs:249 and 276-277, game/hotbar.rs:217-228, game/ranged_input.rs:51-163, projectile.rs:1476-1526, entities/hatching.rs:72-132, entities/persistence.rs:117-194, game.rs:2203-2212, session/eggs.rs:92-150 and game/net_client/egg_throws.rs:62-97 and 178-194. A search of the game code found no spawn-egg crafting recipe.
verification.limits: Source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026, and the calls section at 21d656c2; not play-tested, and the new voices were not listened to. No captures of spawned animals exist yet. Exact spawn counts depend on the terrain around you, so the numbers here are caps, not what you will always see.

blocks.text: As you move, the game checks the 25 squares of ground around you, each about 32 m across. About one square in five is left empty. In the others, one animal may appear, picked from the species that fit that biome. In a given world, a square always offers the same species at the same spot. {{animal-natural-spawning}}

items: Up to 36 wild animals can be around you at the same time. On a server, all players share the same animals and the same limit.
Each biome has its own small group of species. A meadow, a forest and a snowy tundra have different animals.
Wetland fens, flooded grasslands, inland deltas and river deltas can have swans.
Volcanic fields, meteor fields, geyser basins and surface lava tubes have no wild animals.

Each species has a cap. Whales, orcas and giant squid: 1 at a time. Wolves, bears, foxes, crocodiles, lions, tigers and panthers: 3. Boars, goats, buffalo, bison and giraffes: 5. Rabbits, frogs, ducks, salmon, trout and carp: 8. Tiny animals such as butterflies, flies and ants: 10. Most others: 4 to 7.
Fish and other swimmers appear only where the water is deep enough below sea level for their body.
Land animals appear only on natural ground such as grass, dirt, sand, snow, ice or stone. They never appear on planks, bricks, plaster, marble, glass or roof tiles.

blocks.text: New animals do not appear while you are more than 96 m above or below the ground. Over water, the sea surface counts as the ground. Spawning starts again once you are back within 96 m.

Any wild animal more than 180 m from you is removed from the world. Each square gets one try while you stay nearby. It is tried again only after you have moved roughly 250 m away and come back, so animals you hunt are not replaced straight away. Wild animals are not saved: after you load a world, they appear afresh.
Animals you hatched from eggs are set aside instead. They are saved with the world and come back when you return within 180 m. {{animal-spawn-eggs}}
Fish and other water animals do not walk and stand like land animals. Each species follows one of three swimming styles.

items: Whales, orcas, hammerhead and frilled sharks, and flying fish keep travelling in open water. Now and then they glide, slowing to about half speed.
Salmon, trout, carp, catfish, Devil's Hole pupfish and triops swim in short bouts and hold still between them.
Blobfish, comb jellies and giant squid mostly hover or drift slowly.
A swimmer turns away from shores, walls and the edge of loaded terrain before it reaches them. If it has no open route, it holds still.
A hurt swimmer flees at full speed. Salmon, trout and carp also dart away when you come within about 5 m.

blocks.text: You cannot steer wild animals. Their swimming is set by the game and is source-checked, not play-tested in this guide.

57 species make calls. They are cows, pigs, chickens, sheep, goats, wild horses, turkeys, boars, buffalo, bison, deer, gazelles, moose, zebras, elephants, hippos, rhinoceroses, kangaroos, gorillas, gelada and capuchin monkeys, raccoons, sugar gliders, bats, river otters, Tasmanian devils, foxes, wolves, maned wolves, bears, lions, tigers, snow leopards, panthers, seals, whales, orcas, crocodiles, caimans and frogs, and the birds: gulls, geese, swans, ducks, crows, blue jays, peafowl, ostriches, emus, roadrunners, penguins, hummingbirds, sunbirds, toucans, potoos, shoebills and bald eagles. {{animal-calls}}

items: You hear a call from an animal within about 24 m. The closer it is, the louder and clearer it sounds.
At most one call plays every 7 to 13 seconds. When several animals are close, the game picks one caller at a time and rotates through them.
A call follows the animal while it plays. You hear it from the animal's side, and it gets louder or quieter as you or the animal move.
Blue jays and crows call only while morning birdsong plays: between sunrise and noon, near trees, outdoors and not in heavy rain.
Cows, sheep, pigs and chickens rest at night and stay quiet while they rest.

When you hit an animal of a calling species, it gives a short yelp. A blow that kills it ends in a soft, falling sigh instead. Fish, sharks, jellyfish, crabs, insects, snakes, lizards, turtles, rabbits, beavers and giraffes have no voice, so you hear only the thud of the hit.

blocks.text: The game has 94 animal species, from cows and rabbits to whales, giant squid, bats and swans. Each one has its own spawn cap and biome groups. {{animal-species-roster}}

Cow, pig, chicken, deer, sheep, rabbit, fox, boar, goat, frog, gull, goose, buffalo, duck, beaver, wild horse, bear, zebra, giraffe, elephant, hippo, salmon, trout, carp, turkey, peafowl, wolf, panther, tiger, lion, crab, turtle, crocodile, whale, ostrich, kangaroo, butterfly, roadrunner, gazelle, fly, hummingbird, orca, sunbird, gorilla, rattlesnake, hammerhead shark, lobster, Komodo dragon, capuchin monkey, cave centipede, moose, raccoon, blobfish, seal, cockroach, shoebill, snow leopard, crow, alligator snapping turtle, mantis shrimp, emu, platypus, Tasmanian devil, leafcutter ant, bald eagle, tarantula hawk, frilled shark, mimic octopus, toucan, maned wolf, anaconda, anteater, gelada monkey, jerboa, terrapin, comb jelly, giant squid, Devils Hole pupfish, catfish, flying fish, potoo, mudskipper, rhinoceros, sugar glider, skunk, banana slug, blue jay, caiman, triops, bison, bat, river otter, penguin, swan.
The creative catalog has a MOBS tab with a spawn egg for each of the 94 species. The ALL tab does not list eggs. Spawn eggs cannot be crafted. {{animal-spawn-eggs}}

items: Open the creative catalog and choose the **MOBS** tab.
Take the egg of the species you want. It becomes the item you hold.
Hold the right mouse button to wind up the throw. A full wind-up takes 0.7 s and throws farther. Release it to throw the egg.
The egg flies past animals and bursts on the first block it hits. The animal hatches there.

blocks.text: A quick tap is not enough. If you release in under about 0.2 s, the game says 'Too hasty — wind up before releasing' and nothing is thrown.

items: A thrown egg can add animals above the normal 36 limit. An egg cannot hatch while 64 animals are around you, once the world keeps 64 hatched animals, or where the animal does not fit. The game then says "The egg burst, but nothing could hatch here". Eggs do hatch on built floors and roofs.
Hatched animals are saved with the world. When you move more than 180 m away they wait where they were, and they return when you come back. A hatched animal that is killed is gone for good.
In survival, a thrown egg uses one you are carrying. Eggs have no crafting recipe.

On a server, wait for the server to confirm the throw: the game says '<Animal> egg thrown by server'. If the server refuses, for example with 'Wait a moment before throwing another egg' or 'This plot belongs to another player', you keep the egg. An egg cannot hatch on another player's plot.

guides.title: Aiming, camera and on-screen feedback
guides.headline:
Aim it, read it,
feel the camera.
guides.summary: Read the crosshair and looking-at card, steady ranged aim, set the camera effects and follow the status line and collection feed.
guides.lead: This guide explains what the screen tells you while you move and aim, and the camera settings that change how movement feels.

verification.method: Crosshair spread, aim steadiness, the looking-at card, the status line, camera effects, the collection feed and water effects come from the feature ledger, which cites Voxelgame source lines. The numbers were rechecked at Voxelgame commit 0494a0ce: 6 m target reach, Speed FOV 5 degrees reaching full at 16 m/s with a 0.3 s ease, a 7 cm damage dip on hits of at least 1 HP, 5 feed rows shown for 4 s with a 0.8 s fade, and 14 splash droplets. On 8 November 2026 the looking-at section was re-checked at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c: voxelgame-render target_ui.rs:140-147 and 260-291, hud.rs:487-492, menus_ui.rs:181-195; voxelgame-core settings.rs:65, 82-89 and 598-616. On 8 November 2026 the status-line drop sentence, the camera settings route and the character portrait were re-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480: game/item_drops.rs:102-137 and game/creature_melee.rs:71-81 (beneath crates/voxelgame-core/src/); voxelgame-core settings.rs:68-89; voxelgame-render inventory_ui.rs:461-480. Also on 8 November 2026, the crosshair, steady-aim, status, collection, water, held-item and portrait sections and the camera numbers were re-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480: voxelgame-render reticle_ui.rs, hud.rs, hud/survival.rs, pickup_feed_ui.rs, viewmodel.rs, character_preview.rs, player_avatar.rs and inventory_ui.rs; voxelgame-core game/readouts.rs, settings.rs, game.rs, game/audio.rs, game/pickup_feed.rs, game/plant_support.rs, game/inventory_input.rs and game/inventory_qol/presentation.rs.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested, and without screenshots. Judge the bob and dip strength in play. Spread amounts are internal values, so the guide describes their direction rather than exact degrees. The looking-at section was source-checked at Voxelgame dfeb362d on 8 November 2026; not play-tested. The other sections were source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; none of it was play-tested.

blocks.text: The plus-shaped crosshair marks where your aim lands. By default it inverts the colours under it, so it stays readable over sky, grass and stone. In the rear third-person view it moves to the point you are aiming at. It is hidden in the front third-person view and while a menu is open. {{crosshair-and-reticle}}

items: With a bow, rifle or throwable in hand, the four lines spread apart as your accuracy drops. They close back into a plus as your aim steadies.
Other items keep the closed plus.
Raising the rifle's sights shows AIM above the crosshair. Holding [[Z]] to zoom shows ZOOM.

Settings > Interface > Crosshair sets CROSSHAIR STYLE (Cross, Dot or Brackets), CROSSHAIR SIZE (50 to 200 percent), CROSSHAIR COLOUR and CROSSHAIR OPACITY (25 to 100 percent). Adaptive colour inverts what is behind it; White, Lime and Cyan get a dark outline. Every style still opens with the spread.

blocks.text: The spread of a bow, rifle or throwable depends on how you stand, move and shoot. {{aim-steadiness}}

rows: Widens the spread. Faster movement widens it more.
A fuller draw steadies the aim.
Raising the rifle's sights steadies the aim.
A longer wind-up steadies a thrown rock. Dynamite and eggs have a fixed spread.
Narrows the view and slows mouse look. It does not steady the aim.

blocks.text: When you aim at a block within 6 m, a card at the top right of the screen shows it. The card sits just left of the compact map. {{looking-at-card}}

items: The card shows the block's 3D icon, name and distance. The block icon stays still, so thin blocks such as doors stay readable.
The mining advice is one of: "CREATIVE INSTANT BREAK", the recommended tool, or "NO SPECIAL TOOL NEEDED".
An animal gets its own card, with its health. Its model turns slowly.

If furniture is between you and the block, the card is hidden. The hint under the crosshair names the furniture instead, for example "TABLE | BLOCKS TERRAIN INTERACTION". You cannot mine or build through it.

rows: Hide or show the card in the world.
The same setting. It follows you between worlds.

blocks.text: The card is hidden while a menu is open.
Actions report in the status line at the top left. {{feedback-messages}}

items: Mining a whole block reports "Collected <block> x<pieces>". Shift-mining one half-metre piece reports "Carved <block>". Pieces go straight into your pack.
A full pack says "Capacity full; block left behind". The block stays in the world, and "! Inventory full" shows in the lower right.
Opening your pack says "Inventory opened".

Mined blocks throw debris and play a break sound. Mining never leaves items on the ground; in survival, items you drop with [[J]] and animal drops lie there until you pick them up. {{planned-ground-drops}}

blocks.text: A sudden loss of at least 1 HP, from a hit, a fall or a blast, plays a short hurt voice. Voices are at least half a second apart, and slow health drains stay silent. There is no red flash. In Survival, when a blast or an animal hurts you, a small arrow beside the crosshair points towards it for about a second. The camera dip is also a cue. See the camera section below.

sections.title: Camera bob, speed view and damage dip

blocks.text: Three camera effects change how movement and hits feel. Each has a row in Settings > Gameplay > Movement. {{camera-bob-and-speed-fov}}

rows: Walking gently bobs the camera. Turn it off here.
Off or On. On widens the view by up to 5 degrees at high horizontal speed, reaching full widening at about 16 m/s. Jumps and falls do not change it.
Off, Reduced or Full. Full is the default. After a hit of at least 1 HP, the camera dips up to 7 cm at Full and half that at Reduced.

items: Speed FOV eases over about 0.3 s, so a sprint-jump does not pump the view.
Vehicles have their own speed effect, which the SPEED FOV row also turns off.
Only real health loss causes the dip. Hunger, respawn and loading do not.
The dip does not move what you aim at. Aiming and interaction still use your eye position.

blocks.text: The REDUCE MOTION accessibility setting also turns off the camera bob, Speed FOV and the damage dip.
In survival, a small feed in the lower-right corner lists what you gained, for example "+3 Oak wood". {{collection-feed}}

items: Gains come from mined blocks, felled trees, hunted animals, fishing catches, items you pick up from the ground, a chest you break, filled flasks, exploration finds and packed boats or homes.
A gain of an item that is already listed adds to its row.
Up to five rows show. Each stays for about 4 seconds and fades over its last 0.8 s.
Warnings such as "! Inventory full" sit above the gains for about 6 seconds. A repeated warning shows a count, for example "(x3)".
Creative mining, crafting, the creative catalog, home storage and loading a save show nothing.
The feed is hidden while a menu is open.

blocks.text: {{water-splashes}}

items: Wading into water plays a small splash. A fall at hard-landing speed plays a big splash with more droplets.
After you leave the water, walk about 2 m on dry ground before the next splash plays.
Moving through water releases bubbles and a swim sound about every 1.4 m.
Rain makes small ripple splashes on surfaces.
A sailing boat moving faster than about 1.2 m/s throws small spray from its bow. Boats leave no wake.

sections.title: Held items and the character portrait

blocks.text: Held items show only in first person. A block you select is shown as a full-size textured cube held out to the right; plants show as an upright cut-out and doors as a small upright door. Tools are held on the right, and the full-size bow sits just right of centre with its own string hand. With nothing in hand, or with a block you no longer carry in Survival, your bare right arm rests low on the right. Hold left click to swing a tool, bare hand or held block; bows and rifles do not swing. Placing a block plays one swing, and so does a throw. The swing is visual only. A held sailing boat shows no hand. F1 hides held items in the clean view. {{held-items-first-person}}

Press E and open Pack; in Creative, E may open on Build first. Click the figure button beside the pack button; its hint says "Character". A 3D portrait of your explorer appears. Move the pointer across it to turn the model. It shows Creative or your health out of 100, and what you are holding. There are no appearance, outfit or skin options. Remote players in multiplayer use the same fixed explorer model. {{character-tab-portrait}}

guides.title: Caves and geological landmarks
guides.headline:
Caves and geological landmarks
rare rock features, and what each one is like.
guides.summary: Some hills have a shallow cave with one of three layouts. Rare large sites such as meteor craters, amethyst gorges and lava tubes appear on certain ground. Caves are small and bounded, not deep networks.
guides.lead: Caves and landmarks are not on every hill or valley. This page covers where caves open, the three cave layouts, and the landmark sites you can find in the base game.

verification.method: Re-checked on 8 November 2026 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480. Caves: crates/voxelgame-core/src/world/generator/caves.rs:104-160 (the three layouts), 166-237 (one site in 38 of 100 cells of 384 m, none within 240 m of the origin, 132 m radius, 100 m entrance, 32 m site and 10 m entrance heights, the walk-in entrance of current worlds) and 240-248 (the floor stays within 9 m of the entrance floor, itself 2 m below the entrance ground); world/generator/dripstone.rs:9-104 and world/generator/voxel.rs:410-419 (limestone formations in current worlds); world/generator/surface.rs:117-125 (scattered iron ore in ordinary stone); ambience.rs:63-80 (cave ambience). Landmarks: world/generator/regions.rs:109-127 (site biomes), 204-214 (one site per 2048 m cell), 216-277 (radius, exclusions, 20 m height rule and site kinds) and 296-350 (crater, gorge and lava tube shapes); world/generator/structures.rs:41-42,263-295 and surface.rs:523,538 (what lies on the ground); world/generator/voxel.rs:203-222 and map_locator.rs:12-60 (map locator).
verification.limits: Source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested. Sizes are the code's ranges, so a site you find may look different. Sites depend on the seed, so this page gives no map positions.

blocks.text: A cave is one bounded site. Every passage stays within about 132 m of the cave's centre, so it is not a deep network of tunnels. There is at most one cave in each 384 m square, and none within about 240 m of the world's origin. {{caves}}

A cave needs a hill at least 32 m above sea level. Its entrance is cut into the hillside about 100 m from the cave's centre, on ground at least 10 m above sea level. Caves are shallow: the floor never runs more than about 11 m below the ground at the entrance. In worlds made with the current generator, the entrance opens at ground level so you can walk in.
Each cave uses one of three layouts:

items: Fork and chamber: a central chamber with passages that branch off it.
Loop: two routes go around a solid rock mass and meet again.
Pillared hall: a broad, high hall held up by four rock pillars.

blocks.text: Floors climb in walkable half-metre steps. A cave ambience plays when you are more than 2 m below the ground with rock above you.

In caves cut through limestone, worlds made with the current generator have limestone stalagmites and stalactites in the high chambers, some joined into columns. They stay clear of the walking routes.
Caves do not show on the map. They have no lights of their own. The rock is ordinary underground rock, so plain stone walls can hold the odd Iron ore block, as anywhere underground.
Planned, not in the game yet: deeper cave networks and cave maps.

Landmarks are rare sites that spread 220 to 320 m out from their centre, so a whole site is about 440 to 640 m across. There is at most one in each 2 km square. They form only where the centre stands at least 20 m above sea level, not on water or lakes, not within 512 m of the world's origin and not on very rugged ground. {{geological-landmarks}}
The ground decides which site you find:

items: Meteor crater: a main bowl about 185 to 270 m across and 20 to 30 m deep, with a raised rim and two smaller craters beside it. The ground is scorched stone and impact glass, with meteorite rocks of Iron ore and Impact glass. Only on ground that is not volcanic.
Amethyst gorge: a winding canyon 24 to 54 m deep, about 70 to 120 m across at the top, with a floor 15 to 25 m wide. Its dark stone is studded with Amethyst blocks and crystal clusters.
Lava tube: a walkable, roofed passage about 15 m below the ground, up to 8 m high and 16 m wide, with two open skylights. Only on volcanic ground.
Geyser basin and hot-spring terraces: only on volcanic ground.
Cold uplands: ice spires, moraine ridges, outwash plains and firn domes.
Warm, wet ground: karst towers and tepui mesas. Warm, dry ground: spring oases.
Other ground: granite domes, limestone pavements and slate quarries.

blocks.text: Worlds made before the game recorded generator versions (Legacy worlds) have no landmark sites.

Sites are rare. Most of the map has none. To head for one, search the {{map-locator|map locator}} for **Meteor field**, **Amethyst gorge** or **Surface lava tubes**; the other sites are listed under their biome names, such as Geyser basin or Tepui plateau.

guides.title: Volcanoes, water and expedition sites
guides.headline:
Volcanoes, water and expedition sites
volcanic ground, the kinds of water, and the three finds.
guides.summary: Some islands have volcanoes of solid, cooled rock. Lakes, wetlands, springs and the sea each have their own kind of water. Worlds of generation 10 or later have three expedition sites near spawn with a one-time supply find.
guides.lead: This page covers the volcanic ground, the kinds of water you will find, and how to reach and collect the three expedition sites near spawn.

verification.method: Re-checked against the Voxelgame 251b9e46 source on 8 November 2026. Volcano shapes, ages, size limits and the starting-island rule: crates/voxelgame-core/src/world/generator/relief.rs, regions.rs and terrain_profile.rs. Volcanic and geothermal ground and vents: generator/surface.rs, structures.rs and features/vents.rs. Block names: world/block/table.rs. Water kinds, lakes, springs and ice: world/generator.rs, generator/terrain_profile.rs and generator/surface.rs. Water flow: world/mod.rs. Swimming, drinking and damage: world/block.rs, survival.rs and survival/water.rs. Expedition sites, discovery and finds: game/exploration.rs; the Journal labels: crates/voxelgame-render/src/inventory_ui.rs.
verification.limits: Source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested. A site is skipped when its square has no dry, level spot, so some worlds may have fewer than three. The squares and distances are the code's rule; the exact site is somewhere inside its square. Lake heights and water kinds follow generation thresholds and were not measured in a world.

blocks.text: Some islands have a volcano. Each one has one of three shapes. {{volcanoes}}

items: Shield volcano: a broad, low mountain.
Stratovolcano: a steeper cone.
Breached caldera: a wide summit crater with one side broken open. Calderas are always old and worn down.

blocks.text: Older volcanoes are lower, wider and more overgrown; young ones are bare and hotter. A volcano only forms on an island big enough to hold it, never on an atoll, and the starting island very rarely has one. To find one, search for Volcano in the {{map-locator|map locator}}.
Volcanic ground is made of Basalt, Obsidian, Volcanic ash, Lava rock, Smooth lava rock and Magma stone. Hot springs and geyser basins add Mineral crust, Sulfur crust and Geyser stone.
Magma stone glows, but it does not light up the ground around it. Steam vents sit in the mouths of small vent cones in volcanic fields, calderas, surface lava tubes, hot springs and geyser basins.
Nothing here can hurt you: you can walk on magma stone and steam vents and swim in boiling water. Steam vents are plain blocks and do not give off steam.
Molten, flowing lava and fire are not in the game yet. Volcanoes are solid, cooled rock and nothing burns. {{flowing-lava}} {{fire}}
Islands have river channels, inland lakes, marshes, bogs, mangroves, bayous and frozen lakes. Inland lakes lie between about 6 and 56 m above sea level. {{rivers-lakes-wetlands}}
Water only stands at sea level, in lakes and in small springs and pools. A river channel holds water where it cuts down to sea level; higher up the island its valley is dry.

Natural water stays still: rivers do not flow, and water never pushes you. Only the sea's Water can flow. In Creative, the catalog's Water block spreads and pours over edges, and digging next to the sea lets it run into the gap. The other five kinds of water never flow, even when you dig beside them. See {{flowing-water|flowing water}}.
The kind of water depends on where it is:

items: Sea and coasts: Water.
Lakes, springs, oases, inland river channels and cooler wetlands: Fresh water.
Warm, very wet lowlands such as bayous: Black water.
Hot springs and geothermal ground: Hot spring water. The hottest pools are Boiling water.
Frozen lakes: Ice or Black ice, with Fresh water underneath. Frozen fjords: Ice, Black ice or Glacier ice. Under Glacier ice the water is Dark fjord water.

blocks.text: You can {{swimming-diving|swim}} in every kind of water. There is no air meter, so you cannot drown.
You can drink and fill flasks at Water, Fresh water and Hot spring water. Black water, Boiling water and Dark fjord water are not drinkable. {{drinking-flasks}}

Worlds of generation 10 or later have three small expedition sites near spawn; new worlds use generation 12. Each site is somewhere inside a square about 120 m wide, on dry, level ground. The squares are centred about 110 m east, 170 m south-west and 220 m north-east of X 0, Z 0, where a new world starts. {{expedition-sites}}
Worlds older than generation 10 have no expedition sites. If the game cannot find a dry, level spot in a square, that site is missing.

items: Press [[E]], then press [[Tab]] until the Journal opens, or click its tab. The three sites are listed under Expeditions. A '?' means you have not found it yet, and a '+' means you have.
Click a site name to make it your destination. A light beacon and an on-screen marker with its distance show the way. {{destination-beacon}}
Walk to within 12 m of the site and stand on the ground. Flying, sailing or riding does not count. The status line says 'Discovered' and the site name.

While still within 12 m, open the Journal and click Find next to the site. Jumping or swimming is fine, but not flying, sailing or riding; otherwise the game says 'Discover on land; collect nearby without flying or riding'.
If your pack is too full, the game says 'Leave pack space; the find will wait here'. Free some space and try again.
Survey workshop: 16 Alder boards and 8 Glass.
Reed refuge: 16 Reeds.
Stone overlook: 8 Chalk and 8 Basalt.

blocks.text: After you collect a find, the game says 'Find collected | use Craft to turn it into building materials', and its button reads Taken. You can still mine the site's own blocks. In Survival, reaching a site and collecting a find complete the Landmark and Supplies {{survival-milestones|milestones}}.
Each find can be collected only once, and the game saves that it was taken. Finds are for solo worlds: on a server the button reads Solo only.

guides.title: Islands, biomes and world generations
guides.headline:
Islands and biomes
the endless sea, the 92 biomes and why old worlds keep their terrain.
guides.summary: A world is an endless sea of island groups. It has 92 named biomes, and each world keeps the terrain rules it was made with.
guides.lead: This page explains the shape of a world: the sea and its islands, the starting island, the biomes you can find, and why a saved world keeps its own terrain.

sections.title: The endless sea and its islands

blocks.text: A world is an endless sea. Island groups sit in it, and open ocean separates one group from the next. {{archipelago-and-starting-island}}

items: Small islands and palm-ringed coral atolls.
Regional and great islands.
Continental landmasses, the largest of all.

blocks.text: Many islands have up to eight small satellite islets offshore, across a strait of roughly 240 m or more. Atolls have none.

Your world begins on the starting island, at X 0, Z 0. You start in a meadow clearing that blends into the island's own biomes a few hundred metres out. The starting island's terrain is gentler than other islands, and it very rarely has a volcano.

A world has 92 named biomes. They range from meadows, orchards and bamboo thickets to salt flats, kelp forests, meteor fields and surface lava tubes. Every one of them can appear in a new world. {{biomes-92}}

Each biome has its own ground, plants and trees. Forests mix a leading tree with a few others: oak in Dense forest, redwoods in Coastal redwood forest and cypress in Blackwater bayou, for example. Coral atolls grow palms. The animals you meet also depend on the biome. {{animal-natural-spawning}}

The {{fps-coordinates-readout|FPS and coordinates readout}} shows the biome you are in, after BIOME. The {{map-locator|map locator}} can find any of the 92 biomes, so you can travel to one you have not seen yet. See the maps guide for how to set a destination.

Each world keeps the terrain rules it was made with, called its generation. In Create world, the Terrain generation field starts at 12, the current rules. Click it or press Left or Right to pick an earlier generation, back to 1 (Legacy). {{world-generation-version}}

A saved world keeps its generation when it loads, so an update does not reshape land you have already built on. The Worlds list shows each save's generation after its mode, for example 'Creative / Gen 12'.
Expedition sites need generation 10 or later. In an older world, the Journal says "Landmarks appear in new generation-10 worlds" instead of listing sites. {{expedition-sites}}
A generation 1 world cannot contain meteor fields, surface lava tubes or amethyst gorges. Its map locator marks them with * and UNAVAILABLE IN THIS WORLD. To see them, create a new world.

blocks.text: Use the same game build on both computers and a trusted local network. Multiplayer still has limits; it is not complete parity with solo play. {{mp-join-server}} {{mp-menu-lan-hosting}}
Host your world

items: Open **Multiplayer** on the main menu and choose **Host this world**.
Read the join address shown. Other players can choose your world from their LAN list, or type that complete address and port into **SERVER**. {{mp-lan-world-list}}
Keep the host computer on and connected. Opening **Main menu** keeps hosting.

Choose **Stop hosting** to disconnect other players and return to solo play with the recovered world and pack. If the world cannot be saved when you stop, you stay hosted; fix the reported problem, such as a full disk, and choose **Stop hosting** again. If you are sitting or lying on furniture and the space beside it is blocked, saving and stopping wait until you can stand up safely. Clear the space or get up, then try again.

blocks.text: If hosting has stopped but pack recovery fails, keep the game open. **Continue** returns to the repair session, [[F6]] retries, and [[Shift]]+[[F6]] opens a recovery choice. Follow {{guide:saves|Saves and world files}} before discarding any state.
Join a world

items: Open **Multiplayer**. Choose a LAN world or one of your last eight servers, or type HOST or HOST:PORT in **SERVER**. The default port is 27015.
Enter your display name in **NAME**; leave it empty to use your login name, or Player if none is set. [[Tab]] switches fields.
Choose **Join server** or press [[Enter]]. [[Esc]] cancels while joining. Your local world is saved before joining; the server world is kept by its host.

blocks.text: Each player has a separate inventory. Crafting, storage, Survival needs and recovery wait for the server, and the status line says when an action is waiting. Only the world's saved owner has a Home crate; see {{guide:first-survival-day|Your first survival day}}. Boats and some other actions remain limited. A refusal message explains when an action is unavailable.
Press [[Enter]] to type a chat message, Enter again to send it, or [[Esc]] to cancel. {{mp-chat}}
The first server certificate is remembered. If it changes, joining is refused; check the server identity before changing saved trust.
For the separate server program and console commands, see {{mp-dedicated-server}}.
Saving on a server

items: In a world you joined, [[F6]] writes nothing on your computer and says 'This session does not save the world locally'. The server keeps that world. While you host, F6 saves your hosted world as usual.

A dedicated server confirms an action that changes your items, needs or the world, such as crafting, eating, building, storing or respawning, only after it has saved the change. Refusals arrive at once.

If the dedicated server cannot save, the action keeps waiting until a later save works, and it is never carried out twice. If you disconnect while waiting, rejoin and check your pack and the world before trying again.

Near the 8 MiB save limit, any server refuses an action that would make its world file too big, for example 'Crafting would exceed the save budget or saved state is invalid'. Refused crafting keeps its ingredients.

blocks.text: Creative on a server

items: When you join a Creative server, Home, chest and furniture storage move only the supplies you really carry on the server, listed as **Carried supplies**. Free catalogue items stay separate and cannot be stored.
As the Creative host, wait for your pack to be confirmed before using storage. The Home tab says 'Home storage waits for pack confirmation' until then.
The world's saved owner can build, repair, rest at and pack up the Home crate in Creative too. The crate is free, and packing it up gives no boards.

You can move and turn furniture that was paid for in Survival. It is not charged again and still refunds its materials when it is later taken up in Survival. Moving filled kitchen storage keeps what is inside.

blocks.text: There is no fire you can light, spread or put out. Explosions show a brief flash and burst and leave nothing burning. {{fire}}
The FIRE & FOOD crafting tab holds recipes only: charcoal, cooked meat, glass and flasks are crafted there from the pack, with no campfire or furnace to place. {{fire-and-glass-chain}}
Campfires, furnaces and spreading fire are not in the game yet.

There is no lava liquid. Volcanic areas and lava tubes are solid rock: basalt, obsidian, lava rock, pahoehoe and magma stone. Lava tubes are cooled and walkable. Nothing flows, burns or cools into stone. {{flowing-lava}}
Only water flows in this version, so there is no lava pool to avoid.
There are no natural waterfalls. Water you place in creative mode can pour over an edge, but no cascade is drawn and the waterfall sound is not used. {{waterfalls-dripstone}}
Caves cut through limestone do have stalagmites, stalactites and joined columns in worlds made with the current generator. See {{guide:caves-and-landmarks|Caves and geological landmarks}}.

The furniture plans cover chairs, stools, benches, armchairs, sofas, single and double beds, wardrobes, chests of drawers, a bookcase, a wall shelf, dining tables, writing desks, coffee and side tables, floor and table lamps, a cooking stove, kitchen units and bathroom fixtures. Use them as shown in the {{guide:building-basics|Building guide}}. Survival carpentry needs a carried Furniture hammer. {{planned-doors-chests-furniture}}
Each table and desk has a fixed size. For a longer one, place matching pieces with the same woods side by side at the same height: dining tables join on any edge, desks only end to end.
A table lamp needs a solid block counter or ledge; it cannot stand on a furniture table. Sinks, basins and bathtubs hold no water of their own, and there is no plumbing.
Wooden chests and doors are also available; see {{wooden-chests}} and {{doors}}.
Your explorer wears one built-in outfit with fixed colours. There is no skin editor, and no skin import or export. {{player-skins}}
A feature moves off this page only after the game ships it and its source is checked. Its own guide then replaces the entry here.

guides.title: Furniture and carpentry
guides.headline:
Plan it, place it,
set the table.
guides.summary: Unlock carpentry with the Furniture hammer, choose materials, place, move and change furniture, join tables and desks, and put a lantern on a table.
guides.lead: Furniture is built from reusable plans. Pick a plan, choose its woods and other materials, and place it in the world. In Survival you carry a Furniture hammer and pay for the materials when the piece is placed. In Creative it is free.

verification.method: Controls, costs, sizes, refusal messages and server limits were read from the game source at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c and are cited in the ledger rows planned-doors-chests-furniture, furniture-tables-and-desks, furniture-table-displays and furniture-move-and-history.
