verification.limits: Source-checked at Voxelgame dfeb362d on 8 November 2026; not play-tested, with no screenshots and no live server session. Table joins, lanterns on tables and server Undo follow the code and its tests only. The 251b9e46 additions on 8 November 2026 are source-checked only, too.

blocks.text: Furniture comes from plans. A plan is a reusable recipe, not a carried chair or table: choose it once and place it as often as you like. {{planned-doors-chests-furniture}}

items: In Survival, open [[E]] > **Craft** > Tools & arms and make a **Furniture hammer** from two board pieces and one natural stone piece.
Keep the hammer in your pack. While you carry it, the Build tab opens as **Carpentry** and shows every furniture plan. Without it the game says "Carry a furniture hammer to use furniture plans".
In Creative you need no hammer. Open [[E]] > **Build** and find a plan in the catalogue, for example **Table plan**.
Click a plan to select it. To keep a plan on the hotbar, hover it and press a number key from 1 to 0.

blocks.text: With the hammer in your hand, right-click to open the carpentry workbench. Pressing [[E]] while a plan is selected, or while the hammer is in your hand, opens it too.

items: **Seats:** chair, stool, bench, armchair, sofa, sofa section and sofa corner.
**Tables:** table, coffee table, side table and desk.
**Kitchen:** kitchen counter, sink, cupboard, wall cupboard, counter cabinet and sink cabinet, and the cooking stove.
**Bathroom:** washbasin, toilet and bathtub.
**Storage, beds and lamps:** wardrobe, chest of drawers, wooden chest, bookcase, wall shelf, single and double bed, floor lamp, table lamp and wall lamp.

blocks.text: A selected plan shows buttons for the parts it has, such as **Frame**, **Panel**, **Top**, **Basin**, **Upholstery** or **Front**. Click a button to step to the next material, or Shift-click to step back. **Use held wood** follows the boards in your hand, or oak if you hold none.

In Survival, the panel lists each ingredient as, for example, **Need 1, have 3**. Nothing is spent while you browse, preview or cancel. The materials leave your pack only when the piece is placed. If you are short, the game says "You need more of the selected materials". Creative placement is free.

items: A chair, stool, bench or any table costs two board pieces: one of the frame wood and one of the seat or top wood.
An armchair, sofa section or sofa corner costs two frame boards and two wool. A sofa costs three frame boards and four wool.
Cushions come in cream, sage or rust. The colour is only a finish: every colour uses ordinary wool.
Kitchen and bathroom pieces list their boards, stone, marble, clay or iron ore in the same way.

blocks.text: The small **EN** button on the furniture panel switches its captions between English, German and Chinese. It changes no materials.

items: Select a plan. Choose **Place in world** or close the inventory to return to the world.
Aim at the top of solid ground within reach. The ghost shows where the piece will stand.
Press [[R]] to turn it 90 degrees.
Right-click to place it. The status line says "Furniture placed | Ctrl+Z undoes it".
Press [[B]] to put the furniture tool away before you sit, open storage or use a basin.

blocks.text: Wall pieces (the kitchen wall cupboard, the wall shelf and the wall lamp) hang instead of standing. Aim at the side of a wall and press [[R]] until the back faces it; until then the game says "Aim at a wall side; R turns the back toward it".
Placement is refused, and the status line says why, when:

items: You aim at a wall or ceiling: "Aim at the top of solid ground".
A leg would not stand on a solid block: "Every furniture leg needs solid ground". Leaves, plants, doors and chests do not hold furniture up.
A wall piece has no complete solid wall behind it: "The furniture needs a complete solid wall behind it".
A block or other furniture is in the way: "That space is already occupied". An open door gives "An open door stands in that space".
You or another player stand there: "Someone stands where the furniture would go".
Part of the piece is more than 6 m from you: "The furniture is out of reach".
In Survival, you are short of a material.
The world already holds 256 pieces of furniture: "This world has reached its furniture limit".

blocks.text: Select any furniture plan to work on furniture you have already placed. {{furniture-move-and-history}}

rows: Lock the aimed piece for a move. It stays where it is until the move succeeds.
Move the piece to the ghost.
Left click or Ctrl+Z, while moving
Cancel the move and keep the original.

items: A move costs nothing. The piece keeps its materials and contents, and the new spot must pass the same checks as new furniture.

Taking up returns only materials that were paid for in Survival, and only when your pack has room for all of them. Otherwise the game says "Make room for the furniture's boards first". Furniture built in Creative returns nothing.
Empty storage furniture before you take it up, for example "Empty the kitchen counter before removing it".
Stand up before you change a seat. A seat or bed someone else is using cannot be changed.
Select a furniture plan, or take the Furniture hammer in your hand. In Survival the hammer must be in your pack.
Aim at the placed piece and press [[E]]. The panel opens as **Change this furniture**, locked to that piece.
Step through its material buttons. **Pay** lists the extra materials the change needs, as needed / carried. **Returned** lists paid materials you get back.
Choose **Apply changes**. The status line says "Furniture updated | Ctrl+Z restores its previous materials". **Cancel** keeps the original.

blocks.text: Materials shared by the old and new choice are reused, so you pay only the difference. Only materials paid for in Survival come back. The same panel has **Move**, **Rotate** and **Take up**. **Rotate** turns the piece where it stands, if the turned piece is clear and supported. These buttons wait until you apply or cancel a material preview.

Each placement, move, turn, take-up, material change and table lantern is one step. Furniture steps work in Survival and Creative, even after you put the furniture tool away. In the material panel, the first Ctrl+Z cancels a preview you have not applied.

items: Undoing a Survival placement gives its materials back. Redoing it, or undoing a take-up, pays for the piece again.
If the piece changed since, Undo is refused with "Furniture has changed; history kept".
Storage furniture must be empty before its placement or take-up can be undone.
History is cleared when you leave the world.

blocks.text: Furniture stands in front of whatever is behind it. Right-clicking furniture with a block in hand places nothing: the game says "Furniture blocks that placement". Holding left click on furniture stops mining with "Furniture blocks that mining target". {{planned-doors-chests-furniture}}
You can still aim through open gaps, such as the space between table legs. To remove furniture, select a plan and take it up.
Furniture sizes are fixed. Blueprints refuse a capture that touches placed furniture and tell you to use Move or Take up, so they cannot copy furniture or its contents.
Chairs, stools, armchairs, sofa sections, sofa corners and the toilet have one sitting place. Benches and sofas have two. {{planned-doors-chests-furniture}}

items: Put the furniture tool away with [[B]].
Stand on dry, supported ground within 2 m of a sitting place.
Right-click the seat. The nearest clear place is used.
Press [[Space]] or right-click to stand up. You need a clear, supported place to step to.
"Move within 2 m of a sitting position": step closer.
"Stand on clear, dry ground before sitting": you are flying or not standing on dry, firm ground.
"The seat needs a clear, supported standing exit": clear a spot beside the seat.
"All seat legs need solid ground before sitting": the ground under the seat has gone.

blocks.text: Sofa sections join into longer sofas. Match the frame, wool and facing, and place them 1 m apart. A sofa corner joins sections on both open sides; turn the sections toward the open corner.
There are four table plans. Each has its own **Frame** wood for the legs and rails and **Panel** wood for the top. Each costs one board piece of each wood. {{furniture-tables-and-desks}}

items: **Table:** 1 m square, 0.75 m high.
**Coffee table:** 1.5 by 0.75 m, 0.4375 m high.
**Side table:** 0.5 m square, 0.625 m high.
**Desk:** a writing desk, 1.5 by 0.75 m, 0.75 m high.

blocks.text: Join tables into one top

Place two Tables edge to edge on the same floor height, with the same frame and top woods. The shared legs and rails disappear and the tops run together. Tables join on any side and at any turn, so you can build long runs, L and T shapes and wider squares.
Desks join only end to end, when both lie along the same line. A desk never joins a Table, and coffee tables and side tables never join. Different woods or heights stay apart.

Each table in a run stays its own piece. It keeps its own materials, cost and lantern, and you move, change or take up one piece at a time. Each piece still needs solid ground under all four corners, even where its legs are hidden.

When one piece of a run moves, turns, changes or goes, its neighbours get their legs back. If a returning leg or rail would hit a block, furniture or a person, the game says "Clear the table join before separating these sections". A neighbour that is out of reach gives "A connected table is protected or out of reach".

sections.title: Put a lantern on a table

blocks.text: Any of the four tables can hold one red lantern in the middle of its top. Nothing else can stand on a table: ordinary blocks are refused with "Furniture blocks that placement | Use a red lantern on the tabletop". {{furniture-table-displays}}

items: Put the furniture tool away with [[B]], and any tool you hold.
Select a red lantern in the hotbar.
Aim at the top of the table within 6 m and right-click. The lantern stands in the centre of the top.
To take it back, select an empty hotbar slot, aim at the lantern and right-click.
In Survival, the lantern comes from your pack, and taking it off returns it, even if you have switched to Creative since. A lantern placed in Creative is free and returns nothing.
Keep room in your pack to take a paid lantern back.
The half-metre space above the centre of the top must be clear. Otherwise the game says "Clear the space above the tabletop first" or "Another object occupies the display space".
The lantern lights the area around it, as a placed lantern does. It stays on the table when you save.
Moving or turning a table carries its lantern, so the new spot needs room for it too.
Take the lantern off before you change the table's materials or take the table up.
Joined tables keep separate lanterns. Each piece of a run can hold one.
Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo placing or taking a lantern. A paid lantern goes back to your pack, and putting it back uses one again.

blocks.text: The kitchen plans are the counter, sink, cupboard, wall cupboard, counter cabinet and sink cabinet. The bathroom plans are the washbasin, toilet and bathtub. You place, move and take them up like other furniture. {{planned-doors-chests-furniture}}

items: Counters and counter cabinets take a wood, stone or marble top. Sinks and sink cabinets take a stone or marble basin.
The washbasin, toilet and bathtub take a clay, stone, marble or iron body. Clay uses Clay and iron uses Iron ore.

To line up floor kitchen pieces, select a floor kitchen plan and aim at the outside edge of a placed one. A ghost appears 1 m away: hold [[Shift]] and right-click to place it there. A plain right-click opens the aimed piece instead.
The wall cupboard needs a complete solid wall behind it, but no floor.
With the furniture tool put away, right-click a counter, cupboard or cabinet to open its storage. On a sink cabinet, aim at the bowl to use water or at the cabinet below for storage.

A sink, washbasin or bathtub holds no water and has no plumbing. In Survival, right-clicking the bowl drinks or fills flasks only from fresh water already within reach. Without it the game says "No fresh water within reach | carried water kept".
The toilet has one sitting place. Its cistern is only decoration.

blocks.text: The **Cooking stove** plan builds a stove with wooden feet and a stone or iron body. Cooking on it is explained in {{guide:crafting-and-recipes|Crafting and recipes}}.

The same workbench builds wardrobes, chests of drawers, a bookcase, a wall shelf, single and double beds, and floor, table and wall lamps. They use the plans, materials, placing and take-up controls on this page. Their storage, resting and lighting, and the lantern on a bookcase or wall shelf, are covered in {{guide:storage-beds-and-lamps|Storage, beds and lamps}}.
The **Wooden chest** plan refinishes a portable wooden chest. Chests are covered in {{guide:building-basics|Building basics and creative tools}}.

On a server, the game sends one furniture action at a time and waits for the server to confirm it. Only then does the piece appear, move or go, and only then does your pack change. The status line says "Waiting for the server to confirm furniture". {{furniture-move-and-history}}
These work on a server:

items: Placing, moving, turning and taking up furniture in Survival and Creative. In Survival you must carry a Furniture hammer, and the server takes and refunds the materials.

Changing the materials of tables, coffee tables, side tables, desks, kitchen counters, sinks, cupboards and cabinets, bathroom fixtures, storage furniture and wall shelves. The panel shows no price: the server works out the cost and refund when you apply.
Sitting and standing, once the server confirms the seat.
Putting a red lantern on a table and taking it off. No hammer is needed.
Undo and redo, once the server confirms each step. Aim at the table when you undo or redo a lantern.

blocks.text: On a server, chairs, stools, benches, armchairs, sofas, beds, lamps and the cooking stove cannot change materials; take the piece up and build it again. A step that paid or refunded Survival materials can only be undone in Survival, and a free Creative lantern can only be put back in Creative. In Survival, only moves, lanterns and paid steps can be undone. If an answer is lost, the game asks you to reconnect and check the world before you try again.

guides.title: Storage, beds and lamps
guides.headline:
Put things away,
rest and light the room.
guides.summary: Wardrobes, drawers, kitchen cupboards, bookcases and shelves for storage, beds to lie down in, and floor, table and wall lamps for light.
guides.lead: Storage furniture keeps your things where you live, beds give you somewhere to lie down, and lamps light a room without fuel. All of them are built from furniture plans.

verification.method: Source-checked at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c on 8 November 2026. blocks.text: Every piece here is built from a furniture plan. In Survival, carry a **Furniture hammer**, open [[E]] > Build, pick the plan and its woods and check the **Need / have** counts; the materials are spent only when the piece is placed, and Creative placement is free. Press [[R]] to turn the ghost and right click to place it. See {{guide:furniture-and-carpentry|Furniture and carpentry}} for placing, turning and moving furniture.

Costs below are in carried pieces, the same counts that **Need / have** shows. Each part uses the wood you choose for it, and parts that share a wood add up. Floor pieces need a solid block under every foot, and wall pieces need solid wall behind them: leaves, plants, doors and chests do not count, and nothing here can stand on other furniture.

To use a piece, put the plan and any tool away first ([[B]] puts the furniture tool away), stand within 6 m of the whole piece, aim at it and right click. The **Cooking stove** is a furniture plan too; cooking on it is covered in {{guide:crafting-and-recipes|Crafting and recipes}}.

Wardrobes, chests of drawers, the bookcase and the kitchen pieces with storage all work the same way. Each piece has its own storage, holding up to 250 capacity and 64 kinds of item whatever woods it is made from.

items: Put the plan and any tool away and aim at the piece. The hint reads, for example, **Wardrobe | RMB open wardrobe storage**.
Right click. The storage panel opens with your pack on the left (**Pack > click to store**) and the stored items on the right, with the capacity used, for example **Wardrobe: 12.0 / 250**.
Click an item to move one across. Shift + click moves as many as fit.
Close the inventory when you are done. Walking out of reach also closes the storage.

blocks.text: A new kind of item is refused once 64 kinds are stored (**Furniture storage holds at most 64 kinds of items**), and a move is refused when the other side is full (**No transfer: destination is full or item is unavailable**). Moving a piece keeps everything inside it.
Empty a storage piece before you take it up. The game says, for example, **Empty the wardrobe before removing it** or **Empty the drawers before removing them**.

items: **Wardrobe** (Wardrobe plan): 1 m wide, 2 m tall and 0.5 m deep, with two doors. It costs 5 board pieces: 3 for the **Body**, 1 for the **Front** (both doors) and 1 for the **Fittings** (handles).

**Chest of drawers** (Chest of drawers plan, shown as **Drawers** on its tile): 1 m wide, 1 m tall and 0.5 m deep, with three drawers. It costs 4 board pieces: 2 Body, 1 Front (all three drawer fronts) and 1 Fittings.
Both stand on four feet. Right click either one to open its storage, as described above.

blocks.text: While the storage is open, the wardrobe doors swing open and the top drawer slides out. This happens only on your screen and only when the space in front is clear: a block, a door, other furniture or you standing there keeps them shut. With **Reduce motion** on, they appear open straight away. The movement is only for show; the storage works either way. {{furniture-wardrobes-and-drawers}}

Five kitchen plans have storage: the open **Kitchen counter**, the **Counter cabinet**, the **Sink cabinet**, the **Kitchen cupboard** and the **Wall cupboard**. They share the same storage panel, titled **Kitchen storage**. {{furniture-kitchen-storage}}

items: **Kitchen cupboard**: a floor cupboard 1 m square and 1 m high with two doors; its top lines up with counters and sinks. Choose **Body** (body and top), **Fronts** (the two doors) and **Fittings** (handles). It costs 5 board pieces: 4 Body and 1 Fronts.

**Wall cupboard** (Kitchen wall cupboard plan): 1 m wide, 0.75 m high and 0.5 m deep. It costs 3 board pieces: 2 Body and 1 Fronts. Aim at a wall side and press [[R]] until its back faces the wall. Four full solid wall pieces must cover its back; it needs no floor.
The handles use the Body wood until you choose a **Fittings** wood. Choosing one adds 1 board piece to either cupboard.
On a **Sink cabinet**, aim at the lower cabinet to open its storage. Aiming at the basin uses nearby fresh water instead.
Both cupboards' doors swing open on your screen while the storage is open, under the same rules as the wardrobe.

blocks.text: Empty a cupboard or counter before taking it up (**Empty the kitchen cupboard before removing it**, **Empty the kitchen counter before removing it**). You cannot remove a block that holds up furniture, including the wall behind a wall cupboard or shelf: **Take up the furniture before removing its support**.

items: **Bookcase** (Bookcase plan): an open bookcase 1 m wide, 1.5 m tall and 0.5 m deep, with three shelves. It costs 3 board pieces: 2 **Frame** and 1 **Panel** (shelves and top). Right click its body to open **Bookcase storage**; stored items do not show on the shelves.

**Wall shelf** (Wall shelf plan): one shelf board on two brackets, 1 m wide, 0.5 m deep and 0.5 m high. It costs 2 board pieces: 1 Frame (brackets) and 1 Panel (shelf). Aim at a wall side and press [[R]] until its back faces the wall; two full solid wall pieces must be behind it. It has no storage.

blocks.text: Both can show one red lantern on top. {{furniture-bookcase-and-shelf}}

items: Select a red lantern, aim at the top of the bookcase or at the shelf and right click. The hint reads **RMB place display**. In Survival this uses one carried lantern; in Creative it is free.
To take the lantern back, select an empty hotbar slot, aim at the lantern and right click (**RMB take display**). You get a lantern back only if one was paid for it.
Press [[Ctrl]] + [[Z]] to undo the last display change.

blocks.text: The space above the top must be clear (**Clear the space above the tabletop first**). With a lantern in place you can still open the bookcase storage by aiming at its body, and you can move either piece. Take the lantern off before changing the woods or taking the piece up: **Take the top display before restyling or taking up this bookcase**, or **Take the shelf display before restyling or taking up this shelf**.

items: **Single bed** (Single bed plan): 1 m wide, 2 m long and 0.875 m high, with one place to lie. It costs 3 board pieces of the **Frame** wood and 4 **Wool**.
**Double bed** (Double bed plan): 2 m wide and 2 m long, with two places side by side. It costs 6 board pieces and 7 Wool.
**Bedding** comes in Cream, Sage or Rust. Every colour uses ordinary Wool from sheep.
Put the plan away. Stand on dry, solid ground beside the bed, within 2 m of the middle of a place to lie. In Creative, land first: you cannot rest while flying.
Aim at the bed (the hint reads, for example, **Single bed | RMB rest**) and right click. You lie down in the nearest free place.
Press [[Space]] or right click to get up. You stand at a clear, supported spot beside the bed.

rows: Lie down (plan put away, within 2 m)
Space or Right click, while resting
Get up when the way out is clear

blocks.text: The bed needs solid ground under all its legs, room for your whole body on top and a clear, supported way between you and the bed. Otherwise the game says why, for example **Move within 2 m of a resting position**, **The bed needs clear room for your whole body** or **The bed needs a clear, supported approach and exit**. While you rest you can look around and open your inventory; other actions wait until you stand up. {{furniture-beds-and-rest}}

If the way out is blocked when you try to get up, you stay lying down: **Bed exit blocked | Make room to stand safely**. You also get up on your own if the bed is moved, changed or loses its support, if something fills the space you lie in, or if something pushes you.

Resting in a bed is optional and is only a pose. It does not pass time or skip the night, it does not heal, feed or water you, and your Survival needs carry on as normal. It does not set your Home or respawn point: for that, use **Rest / set respawn** at your Home crate ({{rest-respawn-point}}).

Nobody can move, take up or change a bed while someone lies in it (**Leave the bed before changing it**; on a server, **Bed occupied | Ask the resting player to leave first**). If you save while lying down, the save puts you upright beside the bed. If the way out is blocked, the save is refused (**Bed exit blocked; cannot save an embedded player**) until you clear it.

items: **Floor lamp** (Floor lamp plan): 0.5 m square and 1.6875 m tall.
**Table lamp** (Table lamp plan): the same base and lantern on a short stem, 0.5 m square and 0.875 m tall.

**Wall lamp** (Wall lamp plan): the same lantern on a wooden backplate and bracket that hangs on a wall. It is 0.5 m wide and 0.75 m high, and reaches 0.75 m out from the wall. {{furniture-wall-lamp}}

Each costs one **Red lantern** plus 2 board pieces: 1 **Frame** and 1 **Panel**. On the floor and table lamps the Frame wood makes the feet and stem; on the wall lamp it makes the backplate and bracket. The Panel wood makes the base and top. Red lanterns are crafted; see {{guide:crafting-and-recipes|Crafting and recipes}}.

The floor and table lamps stand on four feet, so each foot needs a solid block under it. The table lamp is meant for a counter or ledge built from blocks. It cannot stand on furniture, so not on a furniture table, desk or kitchen counter.
Taking up a lamp you paid for returns its lantern and boards, if your pack has room.

blocks.text: Hang a wall lamp

items: Select the **Wall lamp** plan and aim at the side of a wall, not its top. The workbench hint reads **Wall side | R turns back | RMB on/off**.
Press [[R]] until the back of the ghost faces the wall. Until it does, the game says **Aim at a wall side; R turns the back toward it**.

Right click to hang it. Four full solid wall pieces must be behind it; leaves, plants, doors and chests do not count. Otherwise the game says **The furniture needs a complete solid wall behind it**. The lamp needs no floor.

blocks.text: You cannot remove a block that holds up a wall lamp (**Take up the furniture before removing its support**). To move it, select any furniture plan, lock the lamp with [[Shift]] + left click, aim at another wall side, turn its back to the wall with [[R]] and right click.
Switch a lamp on or off

items: Put the plan and any tool away; an empty hand works.
Aim at the lamp. The hint shows its state, for example **Floor lamp | On | RMB switch off** or **Wall lamp | Off | RMB switch on**.
Right click to switch it off or on.

blocks.text: A new lamp starts switched on. The setting is saved with the world, and a lamp needs no fuel or power. Switching is not an undo step. {{furniture-lamps}}

A lamp that is on lights the walls, floor and ceiling around it with the same warm light as a placed red lantern; a switched-off lamp's lantern stops glowing. A red lantern on display on a table, desk, bookcase or wall shelf lights its surroundings in the same way. The game draws light from at most 16 nearby light sources at a time, so in a room full of lights some may add none.

items: **Storage:** opening a piece asks the server for its contents (**Opening furniture storage | waiting for server**), and each move waits for the server too. You can only use storage where you are allowed to build, not on another player's plot. If the panel says **Furniture storage waits for pack confirmation**, open it again to refresh. In Creative, the left list shows your carried supplies.
**Displays:** putting a lantern on display or taking it back waits for the server to confirm your stock (**RMB place display | Server confirms stock**).

**Beds:** right click, then wait for the server to confirm (**Waiting for the server to confirm bed use**). Other players see you lying down, and two players can share a double bed. A place someone already uses is refused: **That resting position is occupied**.

**A blocked way out:** on a dedicated server you cannot eat while you lie in a bed, or sit on a seat, whose way out is blocked: **Eating refused: Make room to stand up before eating | food kept**. Clear the space first; the food stays in your pack.

**Hosting:** if you host the world and lie in a bed whose way out gets blocked, saving and **Stop hosting** wait until you can stand up beside the bed. Other players can still dig, build and move furniture meanwhile, so the space can be cleared. Then try again.
**Lamps:** wall lamps work on a server like the other lamps. Switching waits for the server. Switch a lamp on before taking it up: **Switch the lamp on before taking it up; history keeps its power**.
**Changing woods:** storage pieces and the wall shelf can change materials on a server; beds and lamps cannot (**This furniture does not support material changes on servers**).
Opening doors and drawers are drawn only on your own screen; other players see the piece closed.

guides.title: Fishing
guides.headline:
Cast a line,
reel in a meal.
guides.summary: Make a Reed fishing rod, cast into open water, wait for a bite and reel in Raw meat. Where you can fish, which fish bite where, and fishing on a server.
guides.lead: Fishing is a quiet way to find food without hunting. The rod costs a few boards, reeds and fiber, never wears out and needs no bait, and every catch is a piece of Raw meat.

blocks.text: In Survival, craft a **Reed fishing rod** in [[E]] > **Craft** > **Tools & arms**. It costs 4 boards of any species, 4 Reeds and 2 Plant fiber, and Wool can stand in for the fiber. Counts are half-metre pieces, as everywhere in the Craft tab. {{fishing}} {{ingredient-groups}}
Reeds grow in wetlands. Plant fiber comes from Wild flax, which grows in some meadows of newer worlds; older worlds have none, so use Wool there. Wool comes from sheep. {{material-sources}}

A rod you craft is equipped at once. Otherwise press [[Tab]] (or [[Shift]] + [[Tab]]) until the status line says **Equipped Reed fishing rod**, click the rod in the Pack, or bind it to a hotbar slot and select that slot. {{equip-tools-tab}}

In Creative, click the Reed fishing rod in the Build catalogue: you take one and it is equipped. Fishing works the same way there, and the Raw meat still goes into your pack. On a server, fishing needs Survival; see the last section. {{creative-catalog}}
Fishing uses nothing up. The rod does not wear out, and there is no bait.

items: Stand by open water and aim at its surface, no more than 12 m away.
Right click to cast. The status line says **Line cast | wait for a bite; RMB reels in, LMB cancels**, and a small cream-and-red float sits on the water at the end of a thin line.
Wait 2 to 4 seconds for a bite. The status line says **A bite! Reel in when ready**.
Right click to reel in. The status line names the catch, for example **Caught a trout | +1 Raw meat**, and you hear the usual pickup sound.

rows: Cast. After a bite, reel in. Before a bite it changes nothing and shows **Waiting for a bite**.

blocks.text: The hotbar shows the rod's state, **Ready to cast**, **Waiting for a bite** or **A bite! Reel in when ready**, with the hint **RMB CAST/REEL / LMB CANCEL**. A bite never gets away: the fish waits on the line until you reel in or cancel.
There is no bite sound, and the float does not move when a fish bites. Watch the status line or the hotbar.

While the rod is equipped it takes both mouse buttons, so you cannot mine, place blocks or hit animals. At a boat's helm the rod does nothing; press [[V]] to leave the helm first. Selecting a block or another tool puts the rod away and cancels the line.
Your cast lands on the first thing your aim meets within 12 m. Three kinds of water take a line: {{fishing-catches}}

items: **Fresh water**, in lakes, rivers and most inland wetlands.
Sea **Water**, in the ocean and along coasts.
**Black water**, in warm, very wet lowlands such as bayous.

blocks.text: Ice of any kind, Hot spring water, Boiling water and Dark fjord water do not take a line. Nor do Water lilies, Kelp, reeds or other plants in the water, or grass on the bank between you and the water: aim past them at open water. Depth, time of day, weather and season make no difference.

items: **Aim at open water within 12 m to cast**: your aim meets nothing within 12 m.
**Fish in open fresh, sea or black water**: your aim meets something else first, such as ground, a plant or ice.

blocks.text: Once the line is out you can look around and walk a little. The line is cancelled if you move more than 16 m from the float (**Fishing line cancelled | too far from the water**) or if the water under the float changes, for example when a block is placed there (**Fishing line cancelled | the water changed**). Opening the inventory does not cancel it.
Every catch is 1 **Raw meat**; the fish only changes the message. Which fish it is depends on the water and on the biome where the float lands:

items: **Fresh water:** carp, sometimes trout. In Pine highlands, Snowy tundra, Snowy peaks, Frozen lake, Frozen fjord and Rocky highlands it is the other way round: trout, sometimes carp.
**Sea water:** salmon, sometimes crab. In Coral shallows, Mangrove coast, Gravel shore, Shell beach and Tide pools it is crab, sometimes salmon.
**Black water:** always catfish.

blocks.text: "Sometimes" means about one cast in three. The catch is chosen when you cast. Fishing does not take animals out of the water, and you do not need to see a fish to catch one.
There is no fish item, bait, rare catch or better rod. The game treats its catch tables and the 2 to 4 second wait as a first version, so they may change.
A catch that does not fit is not lost. The status line says **Pack full | make room, then reel in the waiting catch**, an **Inventory full** notice appears, and the catch stays on the line.

items: Keep the rod equipped.

Make room. Open the Pack with [[E]], point at something you do not need and press [[J]] to drop one, or [[Ctrl]] + [[J]] to drop all of that kind. If you are hungry, eating a Raw meat or Venison from the Pack also makes room for one catch. {{planned-ground-drops}}
Close the Pack and right click again to reel in.

blocks.text: With the Pack closed, [[J]] drops the rod itself, and that cancels the line.
Lines are never saved. Reel in before you leave: a catch still on the line is lost when you quit, load another world or disconnect.

Raw meat from fishing is the same as Raw meat from hunting. In Survival, when you are not full, [[R]] eats the first food you carry, in the order Berries, Venison, Raw meat, Cooked meat, or you can click Raw meat in the Pack to eat it. Raw meat restores 8 hunger and Cooked meat 30, so cook it when you can. {{eating}}

**Cook raw meat** turns 1 Raw meat and 1 Charcoal into 1 Cooked meat in the Craft tab's **Fire & food** section. A placed Cooking stove cooks it too; see {{guide:crafting-and-recipes|Crafting and recipes}}.

Fishing works on a server, including a world you host, but only in Survival. In Creative it is refused with **Fishing on servers requires Survival mode**. The rod must be in your own pack on the server. {{fishing-on-servers}}

items: Each cast, reel and cancel waits for the server. The status line says **Waiting for the server's fishing decision** until it answers. Just after you join, it may say **Fishing waits for your server stock and personal state** until your pack arrives.
The server uses the same water, wait and catch rules as solo play. Only you see your float and line.
If another of your actions is still waiting for the server, the status line says **Wait for the server to finish the current action | catch kept**. Try again once it has finished.

Refusals start with **Fishing refused:**, for example **Fishing refused: Furniture covers that fishing water** when furniture stands between you and the water, or **Fishing refused: Wait a moment before fishing again** after a very quick second click.
The server cancels your line if your mode changes, you die or respawn, or you stop carrying the rod, for example **Fishing line cancelled | fishing rod is no longer carried**.

**Caught a salmon | +1 Raw meat** and similar messages appear once the meat is in your pack. On a dedicated server that saves its world this can take a moment, because the server saves your catch first.
A full pack works as in solo play: the catch waits on the line until you make room and reel again. Disconnecting or a server restart drops the line.
